title: Financial Management for SMEs: Financial Literacy for SMEs
subtitle: Set up your business finances, keep clean books and run a simple Excel bookkeeping system you can trust
summary: Register and set up your business finances the right way, learn the basics of money flow and bookkeeping, then build and use a complete Excel bookkeeping workbook for one month at Bereket Printing and Stationery PLC: daily sales, income and expense trackers, cash, bank and petty cash, and a monthly review.
audience: Owners and managers of micro and small businesses, startups, cooperatives and NGO projects in Ethiopia, and the bookkeepers, cashiers and finance or admin staff who keep their records. No accounting background needed; basic Excel (typing, copying, simple sums) is enough.
objectives: Choose a business form under the Commercial Code No. 1243/2021, and complete registration, licensing, TIN, VAT registration and a business bank account in the right order
Keep business and personal money apart and set simple financial governance rules: who approves, who pays, who records and who checks
Explain money flow, revenue, costs, expenses and profit, and why cash in the bank is not the same as profit
Use source documents, receipts, vouchers and a chart of accounts, and keep records as Ethiopian tax law requires
Build a complete Excel bookkeeping workbook with data validation, SUM, SUMIFS, VLOOKUP and running balances
Record daily cash receipts, cash payments, bank transactions and petty cash, reconcile the bank, and run a monthly review of sales, expenses and cash

runningCase.name: Bereket Printing and Stationery PLC
runningCase.text: Bereket Printing and Stationery PLC is a fictional new printing, photocopy and stationery shop in Piassa, Hawassa, near schools, tutorial centers and offices. Siblings Meseret Alemayehu (managing director, 70%) and Kidus Alemayehu (30%) formed it as a private limited company with ETB 600,000 of capital, and it opened in Hidar 2019 E.C. (November 2026) with six staff. The course follows its new bookkeeper, Tsion Bekele, who sets up the records with cashier Mahlet Girma and the external accountant Ato Yared Wolde, and banks with the fictional Bank A, Hawassa branch. Module 1 registers the company and opens its account, Modules 2 and 3 set up its money flow and documents, Module 4 builds its Excel workbook, Module 5 records its first month, and Module 6 reviews that month: income of ETB 194,182.60 before VAT and a first profit estimate of ETB 19,452.60.

modules.title: Setting Up a Business Financial System
modules.summary: Choose the right business form, register and license it, get a TIN and VAT registration, open a business bank account, and set the basic money rules before the first sale.
objectives: Compare the main business forms under the Commercial Code No. 1243/2021 and their capital rules
List the steps and documents for commercial registration, a trade name, a business license and a TIN
Explain why every company must register for VAT and how the ETB 50,000 cash payment rule shapes your banking
Set basic financial governance rules and keep personal and business money apart

lessons.title: Choosing your business form
body: The business form you choose decides who owns the business, who is liable for its debts, how much capital you need and which records and taxes apply. Ethiopia's Commercial Code Proclamation No. 1243/2021 sets out the forms: a sole proprietorship, partnerships, the private limited company (PLC), the one-person PLC and the share company.

A sole proprietor and the business are one person in law: the owner's house and savings can be used to pay business debts. A PLC or share company is a separate legal person, so members risk only the capital they put in. That protection comes with duties: proper books, a business bank account, minutes of decisions and, above certain sizes, an external auditor.
Cooperatives are formed under their own cooperative law and NGOs under the civil society law, not the Commercial Code, but the money habits in this course apply to them in the same way.

items.label: Sole proprietorship
items.text: One owner, unlimited liability; commercial registration and a business license; no minimum capital stated

items.label: Partnerships
items.text: General, limited or limited liability (licensed professionals only); joint ventures have no legal personality

items.label: Private limited company
items.text: 2 to 50 members; minimum capital ETB 15,000, fully paid into a blocked bank account; shares of at least ETB 100

items.label: One-person PLC
items.text: Formed by one member's declaration with a nominee; minimum capital ETB 15,000; new under the 2021 Code

items.label: Share company
items.text: At least 5 shareholders; minimum capital ETB 50,000; 25% of cash shares paid into a blocked account before registration

regulation.source: Commercial Code Proclamation No. 1243/2021 (as summarized by Ethiopian law firms)
regulation.text: A private limited company has 2 to 50 members, a minimum capital of ETB 15,000 fully paid at incorporation into a blocked bank account, and a minimum share value of ETB 100. A share company needs at least 5 shareholders and ETB 50,000 of capital, with 25% of cash shares paid into a blocked account before registration; bearer shares are prohibited. A PLC needs an independent auditor if it has 10 or more members or assets above ETB 10 million.

scenario.title: Meseret and Kidus choose a form
scenario.situation: Meseret Alemayehu and her brother Kidus plan a printing and stationery shop in Hawassa with ETB 600,000 of savings. They will sign a three-year lease, buy a copier worth over ETB 200,000 and supply schools on credit. Kidus suggests registering the shop in Meseret's name alone as a sole proprietorship because "it is quicker".
scenario.question: Which choice fits their plan best?
options: A sole proprietorship in Meseret's name, with Kidus as an informal partner paid from profits
A private limited company with two members, so their personal assets are protected and both ownership shares are on record
A share company, because it is the most respected form
No registration until the shop proves it can make money
scenario.explain: Two owners with real capital and credit risk need a structure that records both owners and limits liability: a PLC does this with only ETB 15,000 minimum capital. An informal partner has no protection and no clear rights; a share company needs at least five shareholders; trading unregistered is not an option.

lessons.title: Commercial registration and business licensing
body: Under the Commercial Registration and Business Licensing Proclamation No. 980/2016, amended by No. 1150/2019, a business is first entered in the commercial register and its trade name registered, and only then receives a business license for its activity. For a company, the memorandum of association (and articles, where used) is notarized and the capital is deposited before registration.

The license runs to the end of the Ethiopian fiscal year (Sene 30, about 7 July) and must be renewed each year between Hamle 1 and Tahsas 30 (about 8 July to 8 January). A late window runs from Tir 1 to Sene 30 with penalties, so put the renewal in your compliance calendar from the first day.
points: TIN certificate and trade-name certificate
Notarized memorandum of association (and articles, where used)
Identity documents of the owners or members
Lease agreement or title deed for the business premises
Bank evidence that capital is deposited in a blocked account (companies)

items.label: Choose form and name
items.text: Agree the form, members, shares and a trade name

items.label: Memorandum and capital
items.text: Notarize the memorandum; deposit capital in a blocked account at Bank A

items.label: TIN
items.text: Register with the tax authority and get the TIN certificate

items.label: Commercial registration
items.text: Enter the commercial register and register the trade name

items.label: Business license
items.text: License the activity; then register for VAT and start trading

regulation.source: Commercial Registration and Business Licensing Proclamation No. 980/2016, amended by No. 1150/2019; Regulation No. 392/2016, amended by No. 461/2020
regulation.text: Commercial registration and trade-name registration come before the business license. A license runs to the end of the fiscal year and is renewed between Hamle 1 and Tahsas 30; a late renewal window from Tir 1 to Sene 30 carries penalties.

example.title: Bereket's registration file
example.text: In Meskerem and Tikimt 2019 Meseret notarized the memorandum, deposited the ETB 600,000 capital (6,000 shares of ETB 100) in a blocked account at Bank A, obtained the TIN, registered the company and the trade name "Bereket Printing and Stationery", and licensed the activity. Tsion keeps one file with every certificate, the lease and the notarized memorandum, with scanned copies in a shared folder, and has put the license renewal window in the calendar for Hamle 2019.

lessons.title: TIN, taxpayer category and VAT registration
body: Every taxpayer needs a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). The Federal Tax Administration Proclamation No. 983/2016 requires you to apply for registration within 21 days of becoming liable. Your TIN goes on every invoice, contract and tax return, and a supplier without a TIN or business license suffers 30% withholding instead of 3%, so customers will ask for it.

Since 8 July 2025 the Income Tax (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1395/2025 has two categories. Category A covers all companies and other bodies, whatever their size, plus individuals with annual turnover above ETB 2,000,000; it must keep full books of account. Category B covers individuals with turnover of ETB 2,000,000 or less, who pay a gross sales tax of 2% to 9% instead of the old turnover tax, which was repealed.

VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024 keeps VAT at 15% and requires registration when taxable supplies exceed ETB 2,000,000 in 12 months. VAT Registration Directive No. 1104/2025 goes further: all Category A taxpayers, and anyone who keeps books of account, must register for VAT whatever their turnover. So Bereket, as a PLC, registered for VAT before its first sale.

regulation.source: Tax Administration Proclamation No. 983/2016, Arts. 9 and 13; VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024, Art. 12; VAT Registration Directive No. 1104/2025
regulation.text: Apply for tax registration within 21 days of becoming liable; the Authority issues a TIN. VAT registration is mandatory when taxable supplies exceed ETB 2,000,000 in a 12-month period (apply within 7 days), and under Directive No. 1104/2025 all Category A taxpayers and all persons keeping books of account must register regardless of turnover.

scenario.title: A small company with small sales
scenario.situation: Lemlem Haile has just formed a one-person PLC that sells school uniforms in Dilla. She expects sales of only about ETB 900,000 in the first year and tells her bookkeeper not to register for VAT because "we are below the ETB 2,000,000 threshold".
scenario.question: What should the bookkeeper advise?
options: Wait until sales pass ETB 2,000,000 in a 12-month period, then apply within 7 days
Register voluntarily only if turnover passes ETB 1,000,000
Pay the Category B gross sales tax instead of VAT
Register for VAT now: a PLC is a Category A taxpayer, and Directive No. 1104/2025 requires all Category A taxpayers to register whatever their turnover
scenario.explain: Every company is Category A, and Directive No. 1104/2025 requires all Category A taxpayers to register for VAT regardless of turnover. The ETB 2,000,000 and ETB 1,000,000 figures apply to individuals; the gross sales tax is only for Category B individuals.

lessons.title: Opening and running a business bank account
body: A company's capital is first deposited in a blocked account before registration: in full for a PLC, and at least 25% of cash shares for a share company. Once the company is registered, the bank releases it to an operating current account in the company's name. From then on, every sale that is paid by transfer and every significant payment should pass through that account.

Ask your bank for its current list of account-opening documents. Banks typically ask for the registration certificate, license, TIN, notarized memorandum, a members' or board resolution naming who may sign, and the signatories' IDs. Decide the signing rules before you go: for example, one signature for payments up to a set amount and two signatures above it, and mobile or internet banking with separate roles for preparing and approving transfers.
points: Account in the company's exact registered name, never in an owner's name
Written signing rules: who prepares, who approves, and the amount needing two signatures
Monthly bank statement (or online download) for the bank reconciliation
A merchant QR code or account number on the counter so customers can pay by transfer

example.title: Two signatures above ETB 20,000
example.text: Bereket's members resolved that Meseret signs alone up to ETB 20,000 and that any payment above that needs both Meseret and Kidus. Tsion prepares every transfer in Bank A's internet banking from an approved invoice, and Meseret approves it on her phone. When the copier supplier phoned to ask for an urgent payment to a "new account", Tsion asked for a letter on the supplier's letterhead and called back on the number in the contract before anyone approved.

lessons.title: The ETB 50,000 cash payment rule
body: The Income Tax (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1395/2025 requires cash payments above ETB 50,000 to go through the banking system. The limit applies per transaction, per day with one person, or per event, so two cash payments of ETB 30,000 to the same supplier on the same day count as ETB 60,000. A cash payment above the limit is also not deductible as a business expense.

The simple habit is to pay suppliers by bank transfer or check, keep cash for small daily items through petty cash, and deposit cash takings at the bank regularly. Bank payments also leave a record that supports your books, your VAT input claims and any loan application later.

regulation.source: Income Tax (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1395/2025 (as summarized by KPMG)
regulation.text: Cash payments above ETB 50,000 per transaction, per day with one person, or per event must be made through the banking system. Cash payments above the limit are not deductible for income tax.

worked.title: Is this within the cash limit?

rows.label: Total to one person on one day
Limit per day with one person
Result
rows.value: Above the limit: pay through the bank

worked.note: Splitting a payment does not help: the per-day and per-person tests catch it, and the expense would not be deductible.

scenario.title: A discount for cash
scenario.situation: A furniture maker offers Bereket shelving for ETB 58,000 in cash, or ETB 60,000 by bank transfer with a tax invoice. Kidus likes the ETB 2,000 saving and asks Tsion to withdraw the cash.
scenario.question: What should Tsion recommend?
options: Pay the ETB 58,000 in cash, because the discount saves money
Pay ETB 29,000 in cash today and ETB 29,000 tomorrow to stay below the limit
Pay ETB 60,000 by bank transfer against a tax invoice; a cash payment above ETB 50,000 breaks the rule and would not be deductible
Let Kidus pay from his own pocket and repay him later
scenario.explain: The ETB 50,000 rule requires the bank, and a non-deductible cash payment costs more in tax than the ETB 2,000 saved. Splitting into two days to avoid the per-day test is an attempt to get around the per-event and per-transaction rule, and paying from an owner's pocket breaks the separation of business and personal money.

lessons.title: Financial governance basics for a small business
body: Financial governance simply means clear rules for money: who can commit the business, who approves payments, who handles cash, who records and who checks. In a small business one person often does several jobs, so the aim is that no single person can receive, record and approve the same money without someone else seeing it.

Write the rules on one page and agree them with the owners. Good rules for a shop like Bereket's include: every payment has a document and an approval; the person who counts cash is not the only one who records it; the owners review the bank reconciliation and the monthly summary; and any change to a supplier's bank details is confirmed by phone on a known number.

items.label: Approve
items.text: Managing director approves payments; two signatures above ETB 20,000

items.label: Handle cash
items.text: Cashier receives and counts cash, issues a receipt for every sale

items.label: Record
items.text: Bookkeeper enters every document in the workbook the same day

items.label: Check
items.text: A second person reviews counts, reconciliations and the monthly summary

items.label: Protect
items.text: Cash box locked, workbook backed up, passwords not shared

example.title: The one-page money policy
example.text: In their first week Meseret, Kidus and Tsion wrote Bereket's money policy: cash float ETB 3,000 in the till, deposits at least every three trading days, petty cash ETB 5,000 with a ETB 1,000 limit per voucher, every supplier paid by transfer or check from an approved invoice, two signatures above ETB 20,000, and a monthly review meeting within five days of month end. Both members signed it and Tsion pinned a copy inside the cash office.

lessons.title: Separating personal and business money
body: Mixing personal and business money is the most common reason small businesses cannot tell whether they are making a profit. When the owner pays school fees from the till or a customer pays into the owner's personal account, the books stop showing the truth, tax claims become hard to support and a bank cannot judge the business.

In a PLC the company's money belongs to the company, not to the members. Owners should be paid through the payroll for work they do, or through dividends declared under the Commercial Code (dividends carry a 15% withholding tax). If an owner takes cash for personal use, record it at once as an amount the owner owes the company, with a signed IOU. In a sole proprietorship the same withdrawal is recorded as "drawings", not as a business expense.

left.title: Mixed money
items: Sales paid into the owner's personal account
Family shopping paid from the till
No record of what the owner took

right.title: Separate money
items: All sales into the company's Bank A account
Owner paid a salary through payroll
Any withdrawal recorded with a signed IOU
Clear profit, records a bank can trust

example.title: Meseret's IOU
example.text: On 26 November Meseret needed ETB 6,000 for a family emergency and took it from the cash box. Tsion did not record it as a shop expense. She wrote IOU-001 for ETB 6,000, which Meseret signed, entered it in the expense tracker under account 1200 Due from shareholders, and reported it in the monthly summary so that the accountant could advise on repayment or settlement through payroll.

lessons.tip: Put the company's bank account number or QR code on the counter and on every invoice, so no customer ever pays into a personal account by mistake.

takeaways: Choose the form first: a PLC needs at least ETB 15,000 of capital in a blocked account and gives members limited liability
Register, register the trade name, then license; renew the license between Hamle 1 and Tahsas 30
Apply for tax registration within 21 days; every company is Category A and must register for VAT
Run all significant receipts and payments through the business bank account; cash payments above ETB 50,000 must go through the bank
Write simple money rules and never mix personal and business money: owners take pay through payroll, dividends or a recorded IOU

quiz.q: What is the minimum capital of a private limited company under the Commercial Code No. 1243/2021?
options: ETB 50,000, with 25% paid before registration
ETB 15,000, fully paid into a blocked bank account
There is no minimum
quiz.explain: A PLC needs ETB 15,000 fully paid at incorporation into a blocked account; ETB 50,000 with 25% paid applies to share companies.

quiz.q: In what order does a new company usually complete its setup?
options: Commercial and trade-name registration, then the business license
Business license, then commercial registration
VAT registration, then the memorandum
Bank account in the owner's name, then registration
quiz.explain: Under Proclamation No. 980/2016 as amended, registration and the trade name come before the business license.

quiz.q: Within how many days of becoming liable must a taxpayer apply for tax registration?
options: 7 days
30 days
90 days
21 days
quiz.explain: Art. 13(1) of Tax Administration Proclamation No. 983/2016 sets 21 days; 7 days is the VAT registration window after passing the threshold.

quiz.q: Which business must register for VAT under Directive No. 1104/2025, whatever its turnover?
options: Only businesses selling above ETB 2,000,000 a year
Every Category A taxpayer, including every company
Only importers
Only share companies
quiz.explain: The directive requires all Category A taxpayers, and anyone keeping books of account, to register regardless of turnover.

quiz.q: Bereket must pay a supplier ETB 30,000 in the morning and ETB 25,000 in the afternoon of the same day. What is correct?
options: Both must go through the bank, because the total to one person on one day is above ETB 50,000
Both can be paid in cash, because each is below ETB 50,000
Only the larger payment must go through the bank
Cash is fine if the supplier gives a receipt
quiz.explain: The ETB 50,000 limit applies per transaction, per day with one person and per event, so the day's total of ETB 55,000 counts.

quiz.q: The managing director of a PLC takes ETB 6,000 from the till for personal use. How should the bookkeeper record it?
options: As a stationery purchase
As a reduction of sales for the day
As an amount due from the shareholder, supported by a signed IOU
It does not need recording if she repays it soon
quiz.explain: Company money is not the owner's money: the withdrawal is a receivable from the shareholder, never a business expense or a hidden sales cut.

modules.title: Introduction to Financial Management
modules.summary: Understand how money flows through a small business, the difference between revenue, costs, expenses and profit, why cash is not profit, and what owners are responsible for.
objectives: Describe the financial management cycle of plan, record, control and review
Trace operating, investing and financing money flows in a small business
Calculate a simple profit estimate and a break-even level of sales
Explain why a cash balance differs from profit and list the owners' financial responsibilities

lessons.title: What financial management means for a small business
body: Financial management is how the owners plan, record, control and review the business's money so it can pay its bills, grow and reward its owners. In a small business it is less about complex finance and more about steady habits: knowing what comes in and goes out every day, keeping a buffer of cash, and making decisions with figures rather than feelings.

Bereket's owners want three answers every month: Did we make a profit? Do we have enough cash for the next month's rent, salaries and paper? Are we compliant with tax and other obligations? The rest of this course builds the records that answer those three questions.

example.title: A cooperative's first budget
example.text: A women's grain-processing cooperative in Ziway kept no records in its first year and could not tell members whether its mill was profitable. In its second year the treasurer kept a daily sales book and a monthly summary. By month four the members could see that diesel was 40% of costs and agreed to switch to an electric mill, which the records then showed paid for itself in under two years.

lessons.title: Understanding money flow
body: Money moves through a business in three streams. Operating flows come from running the business: sales receipts in, and payments for materials, rent, salaries and utilities out. Investing flows are payments for things that last, such as a copier or a vehicle. Financing flows come from the owners and lenders: capital and loans in, repayments and dividends out.

Only operating flows tell you whether the business itself earns money. A shop can look rich because the owners just paid in capital or a bank loan arrived, and look poor because it bought a machine for cash. Keeping the three streams apart in your records stops these one-off movements from hiding how the daily business is doing.

items.label: Operating
items.text: Sales receipts in; paper, rent, salaries, utilities out

items.label: Investing
items.text: Copier, computers, furniture and vehicles out; sale of old equipment in

items.label: Financing
items.text: Share capital and loans in; loan repayments and dividends out

example.title: Bereket's first month in three streams
example.text: In Hidar Bereket received ETB 600,000 of share capital (financing), paid ETB 246,400 for the copier and printer (investing) and ran its shop (operating): counter and order sales of ETB 223,310 including VAT came in, while paper, stock, rent, net salaries and other costs went out. Looking only at the bank balance falling from ETB 600,000 would have told the owners nothing about whether the shop works.

lessons.title: Revenue, costs, expenses and profit
body: Revenue (income) is what the business earns from its customers, measured before VAT, because VAT collected belongs to the tax authority. Cost of sales is what you spend directly on what you sell: for Bereket, paper, toner and the stationery it resells. Expenses are the other costs of running the business: rent, salaries, utilities, transport, repairs and bank charges.

Profit is what is left: revenue minus cost of sales minus expenses. Not everything you pay is a cost: buying equipment, repaying a loan, paying VAT over to the tax authority and money taken by owners are not expenses of the month. Salaries count at their full cost, which includes the PAYE and pension withheld and the employer's 11% pension, even though those are paid the following month.

visual.caption: Equipment, VAT, loan repayments and owner withdrawals are not costs of the month.

scenario.title: Is the copier a cost of Hidar?
scenario.situation: Kidus sees ETB 246,400 paid for the copier in Hidar and says the shop made a big loss in its first month. Tsion's summary shows a profit estimate of ETB 19,452.60.
scenario.question: Who is right, and why?
options: Kidus: every payment in the month is a cost of that month
Neither: profit can only be known at the end of the year
Kidus, but only for the ETB 33,000 of VAT on the copier
Tsion: the copier is equipment that will serve for years, so it is not a cost of one month; its cost is spread over its life through depreciation
scenario.explain: Equipment is an asset; only its depreciation becomes a cost over time. The VAT on the copier is recoverable input VAT, not a cost, and monthly profit estimates are exactly what good management needs.

lessons.title: Why cash is not profit
body: Profit and cash move apart for ordinary reasons. Cash leaves before costs are recognized when you buy equipment or stock; cash stays in the bank after costs are recognized when salaries' PAYE and pension or withholding tax are still unpaid; and VAT you collect sits in your account but belongs to the tax authority.

A business can be profitable and still run out of cash, or have plenty of cash and be losing money. That is why the monthly review in Module 6 looks at both: the profit estimate and the cash position with the amounts still owed.

scenario.title: A full bank account in the busy season
scenario.situation: An Adama café's bank balance rose by ETB 140,000 in Meskerem, the holiday month. The owner wants to buy a second espresso machine at once. The bookkeeper knows that the balance includes ETB 38,000 of VAT collected and ETB 26,000 of PAYE and pension due next month.
scenario.question: What is the best advice?
options: Buy the machine, since the bank balance proves the café is profitable
Never invest during the busy season
Look at the month's profit estimate and the amounts owed first; ETB 64,000 of the increase already belongs to the tax authority and pension fund
Pay the PAYE and pension late to free cash for the machine
scenario.explain: A rise in the bank balance is not profit, and part of it is owed to others. The decision should rest on profit and the cash left after obligations, never on delaying tax or pension payments.

lessons.title: Fixed and variable costs, and break-even
body: Some costs move with sales: paper and toner rise with every copy printed and stationery stock with every item sold. These are variable costs. Others stay about the same whatever you sell: rent, salaries, internet. These are fixed costs. Knowing the split tells you how much you must sell each month just to cover your costs: the break-even point.

Break-even sales equal fixed costs divided by the contribution ratio, which is the share of each birr of sales left after variable costs. Owners can then ask practical questions: how many trading days at today's sales cover the rent and payroll, and what happens to profit if paper prices rise by 10%?

lessons.title: Financial responsibilities of owners and managers
body: Owners and managers are responsible for the business's money even when a bookkeeper or accountant does the work. They approve payments and budgets, protect cash and assets, make sure taxes and pension are paid on time, keep proper records, and review the figures every month. A bookkeeper can record; only the owners can decide.

Ethiopian tax law makes this personal. The Tax Administration (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1434/2026 presumes managers and finance heads liable, now including for sole proprietorships, and sets a non-waivable ETB 100,000 penalty for each invoice not issued. The positive side is simple: a business that issues a receipt for every sale, files on time and keeps tidy records has nothing to fear and is ready for a bank loan or investor.
points: Issue a receipt or invoice for every sale
File VAT and pay PAYE and pension by their deadlines, every month
Keep books of account (all Category A taxpayers) and file the annual return within four months of year-end
Approve payments, review the bank reconciliation and the monthly summary
Keep records for at least 10 years and renew the business license each year

regulation.source: Tax Administration (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1434/2026 (in force from 30 July 2026, per the Ministry of Justice; provisions as summarized by ethiodata)
regulation.text: Managers and finance heads are presumed liable for the business's tax obligations, including for sole proprietorships. Each invoice not issued carries a non-waivable penalty of ETB 100,000. Tax disputes may now go to conciliation after an objection.

scenario.title: "No receipt, and I will give you 10% off"
scenario.situation: A customer at Bereket's counter orders ETB 4,000 of printing and offers to pay cash if Mahlet skips the receipt and gives 10% off. Mahlet asks Meseret, who is busy, whether that is acceptable for a regular customer.
scenario.question: What should Meseret say?
options: No: every sale gets a receipt; a missing invoice can cost ETB 100,000 and managers are presumed liable
Yes for regular customers, since the amount is small
Yes, but record the sale later in the daily sales report
Offer 5% off instead, with no receipt
scenario.explain: Under No. 1434/2026 each invoice not issued carries a non-waivable ETB 100,000 penalty and managers are presumed liable. A small discount is never worth that risk, and a sale without a receipt also weakens the cash controls in Module 5.

example.title: The monthly owners' hour
example.text: Meseret and Kidus agreed to spend one hour within five days of each month end with Tsion and Ato Yared: the monthly summary, the bank reconciliation, the amounts owed and their due dates, and any decision needed. Kidus, who works elsewhere, joins by phone. They sign the summary page so that everyone knows the figures were reviewed.

takeaways: Financial management is a cycle: plan, record, control and review, every month
Keep operating, investing and financing flows apart so one-off movements do not hide how the shop is doing
Profit = revenue before VAT minus cost of sales minus expenses; equipment, VAT, loan repayments and owner withdrawals are not costs
Cash is not profit: check both, and remember the amounts owed
Owners and managers remain responsible for taxes, records and approvals, and No. 1434/2026 makes that liability personal

quiz.q: Which of these is an investing flow?
options: Paying ETB 246,400 for a copier
Receiving ETB 600,000 of share capital
Paying the monthly rent
Receiving a customer transfer for printing
quiz.explain: Buying equipment that lasts several years is investing; capital is financing, and rent and sales are operating flows.

quiz.q: A customer pays ETB 9,200 including 15% VAT. What is Bereket's revenue?
quiz.explain: VAT inside a VAT-inclusive price is 9,200 x 15 / 115 = ETB 1,200, so revenue is ETB 8,000; the VAT belongs to the tax authority.

quiz.q: Which item is a cost of the month for the profit estimate?
options: Repaying a bank loan
Money a shareholder takes for personal use
VAT paid over to the tax authority
The employer's 11% pension on this month's salaries
quiz.explain: The employer pension is part of the full cost of staff; loan repayments, owner withdrawals and VAT payments are not costs.

quiz.q: Fixed costs are ETB 61,000 a month and the contribution ratio is 61%. What are break-even sales?
quiz.explain: Break-even = fixed costs / contribution ratio = 61,000 / 0.61 = ETB 100,000.

quiz.q: Why can a business have a rising bank balance and still be making a loss?
options: Banks always show balances late
Profit is only calculated by the bank
The balance may include capital, loans, VAT collected or unpaid taxes
It cannot: a rising balance always means profit
quiz.explain: Financing inflows, VAT collected and unpaid obligations raise the balance without being profit.

quiz.q: What does No. 1434/2026 provide for each invoice a business fails to issue?
options: A non-waivable ETB 100,000 penalty
A warning letter only
A penalty of 10% of the sale
Nothing, if the sale is recorded later
quiz.explain: The amendment sets a non-waivable ETB 100,000 penalty per invoice not issued and presumes managers liable.

modules.title: Basic Bookkeeping Principles
modules.summary: Learn the bookkeeping cycle, the source documents and vouchers behind every entry, how to build a chart of accounts, and how long and how well Ethiopian law expects you to keep records.
objectives: Follow the bookkeeping cycle from source document to monthly summary
Identify the main source documents and what a valid tax invoice must show
Prepare receipt, payment, petty cash and internal vouchers, including for a missing receipt
Build a numbered chart of accounts and apply Ethiopian record-keeping and financial reporting rules

lessons.title: The bookkeeping cycle
body: Bookkeeping is the daily work of recording every money event of the business in an organized way, so that the figures can be summarized and trusted. It always follows the same cycle: a document proves that something happened, the bookkeeper records it, classifies it to an account, summarizes the accounts at month end and checks the result against cash counts and the bank statement.

This course uses a simple cash-based system in Excel that a small business can run without accounting software. Every entry starts from a document, carries the document's reference number and is classified with an account code. Your accountant can later turn these records into full double-entry accounts and financial statements.

items.label: Document
items.text: Receipt, invoice, voucher, bank advice or payroll sheet

items.label: Record
items.text: Enter it the same day with its date, reference and amount

items.label: Classify
items.text: Choose the account code from the chart of accounts

items.label: Summarize
items.text: Totals by account, cash and bank at month end

items.label: Check
items.text: Cash count, bank reconciliation and owner review

example.title: An NGO project's field office
example.text: The finance assistant of a water and hygiene project in Arba Minch kept receipts in an envelope and entered them at month end, when half had faded or were missing. After a donor review she began entering each receipt the same day with a numbered voucher. Her next donor report balanced to the bank statement on the first try, and the review found no unsupported costs.

lessons.title: Source documents
body: A source document is the original evidence of a transaction: the receipt from the sales register machine, a sales invoice for an order, a supplier's tax invoice, a bank deposit slip or transfer advice, the bank statement, a payroll sheet, a contract or lease. If there is no document, there should be no entry, and if there is an entry, someone must be able to find its document.

For a VAT-registered business the supplier's tax invoice matters twice: it supports the expense and it is the only basis for claiming input VAT. VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024 allows an input credit only when a valid tax invoice is held; if the invoice arrives late the credit moves to the period in which you hold it, and a missed credit can be claimed within 12 months.

items.label: Sales receipts
items.text: From the sales register machine for every counter sale

items.label: Sales invoices
items.text: Numbered invoices for orders, with the customer's TIN

items.label: Supplier tax invoices
items.text: Basis for the expense and the input VAT claim

items.label: Bank documents
items.text: Deposit slips, transfer advices, checks and the statement

items.label: Payroll sheet
items.text: Gross pay, PAYE, pension and net pay for each employee

items.label: Contracts
items.text: Lease, supply and service agreements

regulation.source: VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024, Arts. 29 and 52; Electronic Invoicing System Administration Directive No. 1142/2026
regulation.text: A tax invoice is issued at the time of supply and shows the supplier's and recipient's details including TINs, a serial number, the date, a description and the VAT amount. Input credit requires a valid tax invoice; a missed credit may be claimed within 12 calendar months. Directive No. 1142/2026 sets up registered electronic invoices with a unique number and QR code; as of October 2026 no nationwide start date had been published.

scenario.title: A handwritten receipt with VAT
scenario.situation: A new toner supplier delivers ETB 11,500 of toner to Bereket and hands Tsion a handwritten receipt that says "including VAT ETB 1,500" but shows no TIN and no serial number. The supplier wants payment today.
scenario.question: What should Tsion do?
options: Pay and claim ETB 1,500 of input VAT, since the receipt mentions VAT
Pay and record ETB 11,500 as an expense with no document reference
Ask for a proper tax invoice before paying; until it arrives, no input VAT can be claimed
Refuse the toner and return it
scenario.explain: Only a valid tax invoice supports input VAT. Asking for it before payment is the moment you have most influence; if the supplier cannot issue one, the full ETB 11,500 is a cost with no VAT credit, and Bereket may prefer a registered supplier.

lessons.title: Receipts and vouchers
body: Vouchers are the business's own documents that sit on top of the outside evidence. A payment voucher records what was paid, to whom, for what, the account code, who prepared it and who approved it, and has the supplier's invoice stapled behind it. A receipt voucher records money received that has no register receipt, such as a customer transfer for an order. A petty cash voucher does the same for small cash payments.

Number every voucher in sequence, never reuse or skip a number, and file them in number order by month. When an outside receipt is genuinely missing, prepare an internal payment voucher: the payee's name, phone and ID number, what was bought, the amount, the payee's signature, and the approval of the managing director. It supports the expense, but never an input VAT claim.
points: Payment voucher (PV): supplier payments, with the invoice attached
Receipt voucher (RV): money received outside the sales register
Petty cash voucher (PCV): small payments up to the petty cash limit
Internal voucher: missing receipts, cash shortages and owner IOUs, always approved

example.title: PCV-006: the plumber without a receipt
example.text: On 28 November a sink leak flooded the back room. A local plumber, Ato Teshome, fixed it for ETB 900 and had no receipt book. Tsion paid from petty cash, wrote PCV-006 as an internal voucher with his name, phone number and ID number, had him sign it, and Meseret approved it. In the petty cash book the line shows "Receipt attached: No", which flags it for the accountant.

scenario.title: The lost taxi receipts
scenario.situation: Biruk, the print operator, asks to be repaid ETB 1,350 for a week of taxi and bajaj trips to deliver orders. He has receipts for ETB 450 and says he lost the others. The petty cash limit is ETB 1,000 per voucher.
scenario.question: What is the best way to handle it?
options: Pay the ETB 450 with receipts on a PCV, and prepare an approved internal voucher listing each trip without receipts, within the petty cash limit
Pay ETB 1,350 on one voucher, because Biruk is trusted
Refuse to pay anything without receipts
Pay from the cash box and record it as cash short
scenario.explain: Receipted costs go on a normal voucher; unreceipted trips need an internal voucher that lists dates, routes and amounts with approval. One ETB 1,350 voucher breaks the limit, refusing all payment is unfair to an employee who did spend the money, and calling it a cash shortage falsifies the records.

lessons.title: The chart of accounts
body: A chart of accounts is the numbered list of headings you use to classify every entry. A simple four-digit structure works well: 1000s for assets, 2000s for liabilities (what you owe), 3000s for owners' equity, 4000s for income, 5000s for cost of sales and 6000s for expenses. Leave gaps between numbers so you can add accounts later.

Keep the chart short enough to use but detailed enough to answer the owners' questions. Bereket separates printing services, stationery sales and order jobs so it can see which earns most, and keeps paper and toner apart from stationery bought for resale. Use the same codes every month, or month-to-month comparisons stop working.

worked.title: Part of Bereket's chart of accounts

rows.label: 1200 Due from shareholders
rows.value: Asset (cash taken by an owner, with an IOU)

worked.note: The full chart in the workbook has 28 accounts. Codes are stored as numbers so that Excel formulas can add up everything between 5000 and 6999.

scenario.title: Where does the laptop go?
scenario.situation: Bereket buys a laptop for the designer for ETB 46,000 including VAT, with a tax invoice. Mahlet suggests coding it to 6080 Office supplies because "it is for the office".
scenario.question: Which account is right?
options: 6080 Office, cleaning and staff refreshments
1500 Equipment, because it will be used for several years; the VAT is input VAT
5010 Paper, toner and printing materials
6070 Repairs and maintenance
scenario.explain: Items that last more than a year are equipment, not monthly expenses; coding the laptop as an expense would make Hidar's profit look ETB 40,000 lower than it is. The ETB 6,000 VAT on the tax invoice is input VAT.

lessons.title: Record-keeping fundamentals and how long to keep records
body: Good records are complete (every transaction), accurate (amounts and dates match the documents), timely (entered the same day), organized (filed by number and month) and safe (locked and backed up). Each paper file should match a workbook sheet: sales reports, income invoices, payment vouchers with invoices, petty cash vouchers, bank statements and payroll.

Category A taxpayers, which include all companies, must keep books of account under the financial reporting standards. Category B individuals may keep such books, but without proper records the tax authority may estimate tax. The Tax Administration Proclamation No. 983/2016 requires records to be kept for the longer of the Commercial Code period or 5 years from filing the declaration; for company books the Commercial Code period is reported as 10 years.

regulation.source: Income Tax Proclamation No. 979/2016 as amended by No. 1395/2025 (books of account); Tax Administration Proclamation No. 983/2016, Art. 17(2)
regulation.text: Category A taxpayers must keep books of account under the financial reporting standards, with separate books for each business activity. All taxpayers keep records for the longer of the Commercial Code period or 5 years from the date the declaration for the tax period was filed.

worked.title: How long must Bereket keep its Hidar 2019 records?

rows.label: Annual return due within 4 months, so filed by about
Commercial Code period for company books (reported)

worked.note: In practice: keep every year's books and documents for at least 10 years, boxed and labeled by fiscal year, with scanned copies backed up.

lessons.title: Financial reporting rules for SMEs
body: The Financial Reporting Proclamation No. 847/2014 sets which accounting standards Ethiopian entities use, overseen by the Accounting and Auditing Board of Ethiopia (AABE). Public interest entities such as banks, insurers and public enterprises use full IFRS. Small and medium entities that meet AABE's criteria use IFRS for SMEs, and micro enterprises are outside the scope.

Where the rules apply, audited annual financial statements go to AABE within four months of year-end, prepared by qualified staff or an AABE-registered professional or firm. Late filing costs ETB 200 per day for the company and ETB 100 per day for the director, for up to three months. Ask your accountant which category your business falls into; either way, the clean daily records in this course are what any set of financial statements is built from.

regulation.source: Financial Reporting Proclamation No. 847/2014 (as summarized by the IFRS Foundation and Ethiopian law firms)
regulation.text: Public interest entities apply full IFRS; SMEs meeting AABE criteria apply IFRS for SMEs; micro enterprises are outside the scope. AABE set final transition dates of 7 July 2023 (IFRS) and 7 July 2024 (IFRS for SMEs). Audited annual statements are filed with AABE within four months of year-end.

example.title: Bereket's accountant
example.text: Bereket engaged Ato Yared Wolde, an AABE-registered accountant, for a monthly fee. Tsion sends him the workbook and scanned documents within three days of month end; he prepares the payroll sheet, the VAT and withholding returns and, at year-end, the financial statements. He confirmed with AABE's guidance which reporting framework applies to Bereket and noted that with two members and assets well below ETB 10 million, the Commercial Code's PLC audit threshold is not met in the first year.

lessons.tip: Ask your accountant at the start which standard, filing and audit rules apply to you, and write the answer in your compliance calendar.

takeaways: No document, no entry: every line in the workbook carries the reference of its source document
Only a valid tax invoice supports input VAT; ask for it before paying
Number vouchers in sequence; a missing receipt needs an approved internal voucher and never supports VAT
Use a numbered chart of accounts and code equipment as an asset, not an expense
Companies keep full books and keep records at least 10 years; the Financial Reporting Proclamation No. 847/2014 decides the standard

quiz.q: Which document is the only basis for claiming input VAT?
options: A handwritten receipt that mentions VAT
The bank transfer advice
The payment voucher
A valid tax invoice from the supplier
quiz.explain: VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024 allows input credit only when a valid tax invoice is held.

quiz.q: A supplier's tax invoice for Hidar arrives three months late. What happens to the input VAT?
options: It is lost forever
It is claimed in the period when the invoice is held, within the 12-month limit
It is claimed in Hidar by amending the return without the invoice
It becomes an expense
quiz.explain: Missing documents move the credit to the period in which they are held, and a missed credit can be claimed within 12 calendar months.

quiz.q: What should an internal voucher for a missing receipt contain?
options: Payee name, phone and ID, what was bought, amount, payee signature and approval
Only the amount and the date
The bookkeeper's signature only
A note that VAT was included
quiz.explain: The voucher must identify the payee and the purchase and carry approval; it never supports a VAT claim.

quiz.q: In a four-digit chart of accounts, which range is used for income?
quiz.explain: Assets 1000s, liabilities 2000s, equity 3000s, income 4000s, cost of sales 5000s and expenses 6000s.

quiz.q: For how long should an Ethiopian company keep its books?
options: 2 years
At least 10 years, the longer of the Commercial Code period and 5 years from filing
Until the next tax audit
Only for the current year
quiz.explain: Proclamation No. 983/2016 requires the longer of the Commercial Code period (reported as 10 years for company books) or 5 years from filing.

quiz.q: Under the Financial Reporting Proclamation No. 847/2014, which framework do SMEs meeting AABE criteria use?
options: Full IFRS
No framework at all
The tax return format
IFRS for SMEs
quiz.explain: Public interest entities use full IFRS, qualifying SMEs use IFRS for SMEs and micro enterprises are outside the scope.

modules.title: Building a Simple Excel Accounting System
modules.summary: Build the nine-sheet bookkeeping workbook step by step: worksheets and layout, a chart of accounts with data validation, the income tracker and the expense tracker, and SUMIFS summaries.
objectives: Plan a bookkeeping workbook of linked worksheets and set up headings, formats and protection
Apply data entry rules and data validation lists so entries stay clean
Build an income tracker that splits VAT from VAT-inclusive sales
Build an expense tracker with totals, withholding and automatic checks, and summarize both with SUMIFS

lessons.title: Planning the workbook
body: A good small-business workbook has one sheet for each job and one direction of flow: documents are entered on the daily sheets, and the summary sheet only reads from them with formulas. The course workbook, sme-bookkeeping-workbook.xlsx, has nine sheets: Instructions, Accounts, DailySales, Income, Expenses, CashBook, BankBook, PettyCash and Summary.

Use short sheet names without spaces so formulas stay readable, and keep the same layout every month: copy the workbook, clear the yellow input cells and change the month dates on the Summary sheet. Month after month you build a history that shows trends and supports a loan application.

items.label: Accounts
items.text: Chart of accounts and drop-down list

items.label: DailySales
items.text: One row per trading day after the cash count

items.label: Income and Expenses
items.text: One row per document, classified by account code

items.label: CashBook, BankBook, PettyCash
items.text: Every movement of money, with running balances

items.label: Summary
items.text: SUMIFS totals, budget, cash position, amounts owed and checks

example.title: Why Tsion did not use one big sheet
example.text: Tsion's previous employer, a Shashemene hardware shop, kept everything on one long sheet with colors for different types of entry. Totals were done by hand with a calculator, and a single sorted column once scrambled six months of data. For Bereket she separated the sheets, used drop-down lists and formulas for every total, and locked the formula cells.

lessons.title: Creating the worksheets
body: Start each data sheet with one header row in row 1: short, clear headings, bold, with a colored fill, and freeze the panes below it (View, Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row) so headings stay visible. Format the date column as yyyy-mm-dd and amount columns as #,##0.00. Color input cells light yellow and formula cells light gray, then protect the sheet (Review, Protect Sheet) with only the yellow cells unlocked.

The Accounts sheet holds the chart of accounts: Code, Account name, Type and Used for. Select the codes A2:A60 and name the range AccountCodes (Formulas, Define Name). Store codes as numbers, not text, so that VLOOKUP and SUMIFS can match them and add up ranges such as 5000 to 6999.

worked.title: Header rows of the main sheets

rows.label: Accounts
rows.value: Code | Account name | Type | Used for

rows.label: DailySales
rows.value: Date | Printing and copying | Stationery | Total sales | Received by transfer or mobile | Expected cash | Cash counted | Over or short | Cashier | Checked by

rows.label: Income
rows.value: Date | Ref | Customer or description | Account code | Account name | Received into | Gross amount (incl. VAT) | VAT | Net amount

rows.label: Expenses
rows.value: Date | Ref | Payee | Description | Account code | Account name | Goods or services | Paid from | Document | Net amount | VAT | Total | WHT withheld | Amount paid | Check

rows.label: CashBook and BankBook
rows.value: Date | Ref | Description | In (deposits) | Out (payments) | Balance

rows.label: PettyCash
rows.value: Date | Voucher No. | Description | Account code | Receipt attached | Top-up received | Paid out | Balance

worked.note: Columns A to I on Income and A to O on Expenses are used exactly as listed, so the formulas in the next lessons point to the right columns.

lessons.tip: Turn on File, Options, Save, AutoRecover every 5 minutes, and save a dated copy at the end of each day.

lessons.title: Data entry structure and data validation
body: Excel can only add up what is entered consistently. Use one row per document, one value per cell, and no blank rows, merged cells or subtotals inside the data. Put dates in a date column, amounts as plain numbers without "ETB" typed in, and choose account codes from a list rather than typing names.

Data validation (Data, Data Validation) enforces these rules. On Income column D choose List with source =AccountCodes; on Received into choose List with source Counter,Bank,Cash; on Expenses Paid from use Cash,Bank,Petty cash, and Document use Tax invoice,Receipt,Internal voucher,Payroll sheet,Bank statement. Set amounts to Decimal greater than 0, and dates to Date between =Summary!$B$2 and =Summary!$B$3 so a mistyped year is refused.

right.title: Ready for SUMIFS
items: One row per document, no gaps
All totals on the Summary sheet

scenario.title: Three spellings of one account
scenario.situation: Before data validation, Mahlet entered paper purchases as "Paper", "paper and toner" and "5010". The summary formula that adds account 5010 shows ETB 16,000, but Tsion knows ETB 52,650 of paper and materials were bought in Hidar.
scenario.question: What is the best fix?
options: Correct the entries to code 5010 and add a data validation list =AccountCodes on the code column so only listed codes can be entered
Add the missing amounts to the summary by hand each month
Use a separate formula for each spelling
Delete the old rows and start again next month
scenario.explain: Clean codes plus validation fix both the past and the future. Hand adjustments and one formula per spelling hide the problem and break again, and deleting rows destroys the records.

lessons.title: The income tracker
body: The Income sheet lists every income document: each trading day's counter sales, taken from the daily sales report as two rows (4010 printing and 4020 stationery), and every order invoice paid by transfer. Bereket's prices include VAT, so the bookkeeper types the gross amount the customer paid and lets Excel split out the VAT.

The VAT inside a VAT-inclusive amount is gross x 15 / 115, rounded to cents: in H2 type =IF(G2="","",ROUND(G2*15/115,2)), and in I2 the net amount =IF(G2="","",G2-H2). The account name in E2 comes from the chart with =IF(D2="","",VLOOKUP(D2,Accounts!$A$2:$B$60,2,FALSE)). Copy the formulas down to row 500 so new rows calculate automatically.

worked.title: Sample rows from Bereket's income tracker

rows.label: 2026-11-27 | INV-0002 | Exam booklets, Selam Tutorial Center | 4030 | Bank | 9,200.00

worked.note: Check one row by hand each month: 5,980 x 15 / 115 = 780, and 5,980 minus 780 = 5,200.

example.title: The 15% mistake
example.text: In her first week Mahlet calculated VAT on counter sales as 15% of the gross amount: 5,980 x 15% = ETB 897. That overstates VAT by ETB 117 on one line, and over a month it would have overstated output VAT by thousands of birr. The 15/115 formula gives the VAT already inside a VAT-inclusive price.

lessons.title: The expense tracker
body: The Expenses sheet lists every payment, whatever its source: bank transfers, checks, cash from the till and petty cash vouchers. For each row type the net amount and the VAT from the supplier's tax invoice (0 if there is none). Total in L2 is =IF(J2="","",J2+K2); Amount paid in N2 is =IF(J2="","",L2-M2), where M is any withholding tax the accountant deducts.

Column O does the checking for you: =IF(J2="","",IF(AND(K2>0,I2<>"Tax invoice"),"No input VAT without a tax invoice",IF(AND(M2=0,OR(AND(G2="Goods",J2>20000),AND(G2="Services",J2>10000))),"Check withholding",IF(AND(H2="Cash",N2>50000),"Above ETB 50,000: pay through the bank","")))). Add conditional formatting so any message shows in red, and clear every red cell before month end.

worked.title: Sample rows from Bereket's expense tracker

rows.label: 2026-11-10 | INV-0457 | Copier and printer | 1500 | Goods | Bank | Tax invoice
2026-11-10 | RCT-112 | Shop rent, Hidar | 6020 | Other | Bank | Receipt
2026-11-11 | INV-2231 | A4 paper and toner | 5010 | Goods | Bank | Tax invoice
2026-11-26 | IOU-001 | Cash taken by Meseret | 1200 | Other | Cash | Internal voucher
2026-11-28 | PCV-006 | Plumber, receipt missing | 6070 | Services | Petty cash | Internal voucher

worked.note: The copier row would show "Check withholding" until the accountant entered ETB 6,600 (3% of the ETB 220,000 price before VAT) in column M.

regulation.source: Income Tax Proclamation No. 979/2016, Art. 97 (old Art. 92) as amended by No. 1395/2025, in force 7 August 2025
regulation.text: Companies, government agencies and NGOs withhold 3% from domestic payments for goods above ETB 20,000 and for services above ETB 10,000 per transaction or contract (micro enterprises are excluded from the duty). The rate is 30% if the supplier has no TIN or business license. Confirm the base and the remittance deadline with your accountant or the Ministry of Revenues.

scenario.title: VAT on a receipt
scenario.situation: Tsion enters the landlord's rent receipt of ETB 25,000. Mahlet, helping, types ETB 3,750 in the VAT column "because everything has 15% VAT". The Document column says Receipt, and column O turns red.
scenario.question: What should Tsion do?
options: Change the Document column to Tax invoice so the warning disappears
Keep the VAT and delete the check formula
Split the rent into two rows to avoid the warning
Set VAT to 0: the landlord issued a receipt, not a tax invoice, so there is no input VAT to claim
scenario.explain: Input VAT exists only on a valid tax invoice. Changing the document type or removing the check would put a false VAT claim in the records, and splitting the row changes nothing.

lessons.title: Summarizing with SUM and SUMIFS
body: SUM adds a range: =SUM(DailySales!D2:D40) gives the month's total counter sales. SUMIFS adds only the rows that meet conditions: =SUMIFS(sum range, criteria range 1, criterion 1, criteria range 2, criterion 2, ...). On the Summary sheet, the net income for the account code in A6, for the month whose start and end dates are in B2 and B3, is =SUMIFS(Income!$I$2:$I$500,Income!$D$2:$D$500,$A6,Income!$A$2:$A$500,">="&$B$2,Income!$A$2:$A$500,"<="&$B$3).

The dollar signs fix the ranges so you can copy the formula down to the next account. Use ranges that reach row 500, not just the rows you have today, or next month's new rows will be left out. The same pattern on Expenses!$J (net) and Expenses!$K (VAT) gives costs and input VAT by account, and a range test such as ">=5000" and "<7000" adds all costs and expenses at once.

worked.title: What Bereket's Summary formulas return for Hidar
worked.note: The check line proves that every birr in the daily sales report reached the income tracker.

scenario.title: The formula that stopped growing
scenario.situation: In Tahsas the Summary shows stationery sales of only ETB 38,000, about half the usual. Tsion finds the formula =SUMIFS(Income!I2:I60,Income!D2:D60,A7), written when Hidar's income tracker had 52 rows. With the Genna orders, Tahsas has 74 rows, running to row 75.
scenario.question: What is the best correction?
options: Type the correct total over the formula
Rewrite it as =SUMIFS(Income!$I$2:$I$500,Income!$D$2:$D$500,$A7, plus the two date conditions) and copy it to the other accounts
Delete old Hidar rows so Tahsas fits in rows 2 to 60
Move to a new workbook every time the rows run out
scenario.explain: Full, fixed ranges with date criteria work for every month without editing. Typing over formulas, deleting history or restarting the file all destroy the reliability of the records.

takeaways: One sheet per job, entries on the daily sheets, totals only on the Summary sheet
One header row, frozen panes, number formats, yellow inputs, gray locked formulas
Data validation lists for codes, payment methods and documents keep entries clean
VAT inside a VAT-inclusive amount is ROUND(gross x 15 / 115, 2), not 15% of gross
SUMIFS with fixed ranges to row 500 and date criteria gives monthly totals by account; check columns catch VAT, withholding and cash-limit errors

quiz.q: A counter sale of ETB 2,300 includes 15% VAT. Which formula gives the VAT in H2 if G2 holds 2,300?
quiz.explain: The VAT inside a VAT-inclusive price is 15/115 of it: ETB 300 here; 15% of gross would give ETB 345.

quiz.q: Why are account codes stored as numbers on the Accounts sheet?
options: Because Excel cannot store text
So VLOOKUP and SUMIFS match them and ranges like 5000 to 6999 can be added
To make the sheet look neater
Numbers take less memory
quiz.explain: Mixing text and numbers breaks lookups and range criteria; numeric codes work in every formula.

quiz.q: Which data validation stops an entry dated in the wrong month?
options: List =AccountCodes
Decimal greater than 0
Date between =Summary!$B$2 and =Summary!$B$3
Text length equal to 10
quiz.explain: A date rule tied to the month's start and end dates refuses dates outside the month.

quiz.q: In the expense tracker, net is ETB 16,000, VAT ETB 2,400 and withholding ETB 0. What does N2 =L2-M2 show?
quiz.explain: Total L2 = 16,000 + 2,400 = 18,400, and with no withholding the amount paid is ETB 18,400.

quiz.q: What does the criterion ">="&$B$2 do inside SUMIFS?
options: Adds B2 to the total
Excludes the row in B2
Sorts the data by date
Includes only rows dated on or after the date in B2
quiz.explain: The & joins the operator to the date in B2, so SUMIFS keeps rows with dates from the month start.

quiz.q: Column O shows "No input VAT without a tax invoice". What caused it?
options: The amount is above ETB 50,000
The account code is missing
VAT was entered on a row whose document is not a tax invoice
The row has withholding tax
quiz.explain: The first test in O2 flags any VAT amount where the Document column is not Tax invoice.

modules.title: Daily Financial Data Entry
modules.summary: Record a full day of money: counter sales and the cash count, cash payments, bank deposits and transfers, petty cash, and the month-end bank reconciliation.
objectives: Follow a daily routine that opens, counts, records and deposits cash the same day
Record cash receipts with a daily sales report and handle cash over and short
Record cash payments and bank transactions with running balances in the cash book and bank book
Run an imprest petty cash system and prepare a monthly bank reconciliation

lessons.title: The daily money routine
body: Good books are built one day at a time. At Bereket the day starts with a ETB 3,000 change float in the cash box, counted by Mahlet and checked by Tsion. During the day every sale gets a receipt from the sales register machine, and every payment gets a voucher. At closing, the machine's day-end report gives the sales by type, Mahlet counts the cash, and Tsion completes the daily sales report and enters the day in the workbook.

Leaving entries for the weekend is how errors and missing receipts creep in. Ten to fifteen minutes at the end of each day keeps the cash box, the bank and the books in agreement, and makes the month-end close a short check rather than a week of searching.

items.label: 08:00 Open
items.text: Count and sign for the ETB 3,000 float; check yesterday's deposit slip

items.label: During the day
items.text: Receipt for every sale; voucher for every payment; transfers checked on the merchant app

items.label: 17:30 Close
items.text: Day-end report from the sales register; cash count by cashier, checked by bookkeeper

items.label: 17:45 Record
items.text: DailySales row, two Income rows, CashBook and BankBook entries, any vouchers

items.label: Deposit day
items.text: Bank everything above the float at least every three trading days

example.title: A tailor's evening habit
example.text: Ato Habtamu runs a three-person tailoring shop in Bahir Dar as a sole proprietor. He used to keep takings in a drawer and "do the books" once a month. Now he writes the day's sales and expenses in a simple sheet each evening before closing and banks the cash twice a week. After three months he could show Bank A a clear sales history and obtained a working capital loan for fabric.

lessons.title: Cash receipts and the daily sales report
body: The daily sales report (DailySales sheet) is the control on counter sales. Enter the day's printing and stationery sales from the day-end report, then the transfers and mobile payments shown on the merchant report. Excel calculates the total =B2+C2, the cash that should be in the box =D2-E2, and the difference between cash counted and expected =G2-F2.

A small difference happens in any busy shop, but it must be recorded honestly, never hidden. Before accepting a shortage, check the usual causes: a transfer rung up as cash, a sale entered twice, or change given wrongly. A real shortage is recorded in the expense tracker as account 6950 Cash over and short, with an internal voucher signed by the cashier, and repeated shortages are discussed with the owner.

regulation.source: Council of Ministers Regulation No. 139/2007 (sales register machines); Tax Administration (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1434/2026
regulation.text: Businesses use accredited sales register machines to issue receipts under Regulation No. 139/2007, with electronic invoicing being added under Directive No. 1142/2026. Each invoice not issued carries a non-waivable ETB 100,000 penalty under No. 1434/2026.

worked.title: Bereket's daily sales report, 19 November 2026

rows.label: Received by transfer or mobile (merchant report)

worked.note: Income tracker: 3,810 (4010) and 3,320 (4020). Cash book: in 4,720, then out 150 as "Cash short", which also goes in the expense tracker as account 6950. Bank book: in 2,410.

scenario.title: "I will put it back from my own money"
scenario.situation: At closing the cash count is ETB 600 short. Mahlet is upset and offers to put ETB 600 from her own purse into the box so the report balances. She says it happened because the lunch hour was very busy.
scenario.question: What should Tsion do first?
options: Accept Mahlet's ETB 600 so the report balances and the owners are not worried
Compare the merchant report with the sales register to see if a transfer was rung up as cash, then record any real shortage on a signed internal voucher
Change the cash counted figure to match the expected cash
Deduct ETB 600 from Mahlet's salary without telling the owners
scenario.explain: Most shortages have a recording cause, and the merchant report shows it quickly. A shortage that is covered privately or typed away hides the problem; salary deductions need the owners' decision and fair procedure, not a bookkeeper's shortcut.

lessons.title: Cash payments and the cash book
body: The cash book (CashBook sheet) records every movement in and out of the cash box: cash sales from the daily sales report, cash payments, deposits to the bank, petty cash top-ups and any owner IOU. Each line has a date, a reference and the amount in or out. The running balance in F3 is =IF(A3="","",F2+D3-E3): yesterday's balance plus today's cash in minus cash out.

Pay cash only for small, approved, documented items, and never above the ETB 50,000 limit. Cash paid out for an expense or an owner's IOU (ink from a small trader, a cash shortage, IOU-001 coded 1200) also goes in the expense tracker. A movement between cash, bank and petty cash is not an expense: it goes only in the money books. At month end the closing balance =SUM(D2:D500)-SUM(E2:E500) must equal the cash counted in the box.

worked.title: Bereket's cash book, 25 to 28 November

rows.label: 25 Nov | DS-04 | Cash deposited at Bank A | out 17,610
26 Nov | IOU-001 | Meseret, personal use | out 6,000
27 Nov | RCT-0311 | Printer ink refill | out 3,400
28 Nov | DS-05 | Cash deposited at Bank A | out 7,690

worked.note: Every deposit brings the box back to the ETB 3,000 float. The IOU made the 28 November deposit smaller, which is exactly why it must be recorded and reviewed.

regulation.source: Income Tax (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1395/2025 (as summarized by KPMG)
regulation.text: Cash payments above ETB 50,000 per transaction, per day with one person, or per event must go through the banking system, and cash payments above that limit are not deductible for income tax.

example.title: The trader without a tax invoice
example.text: On 27 November the toner supplier was out of stock and Biruk bought an ink refill for ETB 3,400 from a small trader in Piassa, paying cash from the box with Meseret's approval. The trader gave a receipt but is not VAT-registered, so Tsion entered it with Document "Receipt" and VAT 0. It is a valid cost, but with no input VAT, which is one reason Bereket prefers its registered suppliers.

lessons.title: Bank transactions and the bank book
body: The bank book (BankBook sheet) is your own record of the Bank A account, kept the same way as the cash book: deposits in, payments out and a running balance. Record cash deposits from the deposit slip, customer transfers from the merchant report or transfer advice, supplier payments from the payment voucher, checks on the day you write them, and salaries from the payroll sheet.

Check the merchant or mobile app each day against the transfers entered in the daily sales report, so a customer cannot claim to have paid when the money never arrived. Keep the check book locked, write checks only against an approved payment voucher and record each check number in the reference column, because a check you have written reduces your balance even if the supplier has not yet cashed it.
points: Deposits: cash from the cash book, with the deposit slip number (DS-01, DS-02 ...)
Transfers in: daily merchant total and each order invoice paid
Payments: transfers and checks with the voucher or check number
Statement-only items (charges, interest): entered when the statement arrives

example.title: A screenshot is not a payment
example.text: A customer collecting ETB 5,750 of printed brochures showed Mahlet a phone screenshot of a transfer. Bereket's rule is to check the merchant app before releasing goods, and no transfer had arrived. The customer called his bank and found the transfer had failed; he paid again and the money showed up in the app within minutes. Without the check, Bereket would have lost the sale.

lessons.tip: Download the bank statement every week, not only at month end, so differences are small and fresh when you look for them.

lessons.title: The bank reconciliation
body: A bank reconciliation proves that your bank book and the bank's statement agree once timing differences are explained. Deposits in transit (recorded by you, not yet credited by the bank) and outstanding checks (written by you, not yet cashed) are normal timing items. Charges, interest or transfers that appear only on the statement must be entered in your bank book first.

Do it every month within a few days of month end, and have the owner review and sign it. A difference that cannot be explained is never "rounded away": it is either an error to correct or a warning sign to investigate, such as an unauthorized payment.

items.label: Tick
items.text: Match each statement line to the bank book

items.label: Record
items.text: Enter statement-only items such as charges in the bank book and expense tracker

items.label: List timing items
items.text: Deposits in transit and outstanding checks

items.label: Adjust
items.text: Statement + deposits in transit - outstanding checks

items.label: Agree and sign
items.text: Adjusted balance = bank book balance; owner signs

rows.label: Add: deposit in transit DS-08 (credited 10 December)
Less: outstanding check No. 000004, Tabor Paper
