worked.note: In the workbook, the charges are entered in the bank book and the expense tracker first; then the BankBook formula =I3+I4-I5 minus the book balance shows 0.

scenario.title: An unknown credit of ETB 4,600
scenario.situation: Reconciling Tahsas, Tsion finds a credit of ETB 4,600 on the statement with the narration "Transfer, A. Getachew" that is not in the bank book. No invoice to that name exists and the adjusted balances differ by exactly ETB 4,600.
scenario.question: What should she do?
options: Record it as printing income so the reconciliation balances
Ignore it, because extra money in the account is not a problem
Transfer it back immediately without asking anyone
Check the merchant report and order book for that customer and amount, and hold it as an unidentified receipt until confirmed; never record it as income by guesswork
scenario.explain: An unexplained credit may be a customer's advance, a payment meant for another business or an error. It is identified first; recording it as income could overstate sales and VAT, and sending it back blindly could refund a genuine customer.

lessons.title: Petty cash management
body: Petty cash is a small, fixed float for minor payments, kept separately from the till by one named custodian. Bereket uses the imprest system: a float of ETB 5,000, a limit of ETB 1,000 per voucher, and a top-up from the cash box that equals exactly the vouchers paid. At any moment, cash in the tin plus vouchers paid since the last top-up must equal ETB 5,000.

Every payment needs a numbered petty cash voucher with the receipt attached, or an approved internal voucher when the receipt is missing. The petty cash book (PettyCash sheet) keeps a running balance =IF(A3="","",H2+F3-G3), and each voucher is also entered in the expense tracker with Paid from "Petty cash", so the costs reach the right accounts.

items.label: Top up by the vouchers' total

worked.title: Bereket's petty cash count, 9 December 2026

rows.label: Vouchers since the 2 December top-up: PCV-007 ETB 350, PCV-008 ETB 250
Top-up needed from the cash box

worked.note: The first top-up, on 2 December, was ETB 2,700 against vouchers PCV-001 to PCV-006.

scenario.title: An IOU in the petty cash tin
scenario.situation: At the weekly count the petty cash tin holds ETB 3,100 in cash, vouchers of ETB 1,400 and a note from Abel saying "Borrowed ETB 500, will return on payday".
scenario.question: What should Tsion do?
options: Treat Abel's note as a voucher and top up ETB 1,900
Report the ETB 500 personal loan to Meseret, ask Abel to repay it now, and remind staff that petty cash is never lent
Top up ETB 1,400 and leave the note in the tin until payday
Record ETB 500 as cash short
scenario.explain: Petty cash pays business costs against vouchers; it is not a staff loan fund. Cash ETB 3,100 + vouchers ETB 1,400 + the ETB 500 note make ETB 5,000, so nothing is missing, but topping up for the note or calling it a shortage would put a personal loan into the business accounts.

takeaways: Count, record and deposit every day; keep the till float at ETB 3,000 and bank the rest
The daily sales report proves counter sales: expected cash = total sales - transfers, and differences are recorded honestly
Cash book and bank book keep running balances =F2+D3-E3; transfers between cash and bank are never income or expense
Reconcile the bank every month: statement + deposits in transit - outstanding checks = bank book after charges
Imprest petty cash: cash in the tin plus vouchers always equals the float

quiz.q: Total sales are ETB 8,600 and transfers ETB 2,350. Cash counted is ETB 6,250. What is the over or short?
options: ETB 0
ETB 250
quiz.explain: Expected cash = 8,600 - 2,350 = 6,250, so counted minus expected is 0.

quiz.q: Which entry belongs in the cash book and bank book only, not in the expense tracker?
options: Paying a small trader for an ink refill
A cash shortage at the daily count
Depositing cash takings at Bank A
An owner's IOU for cash taken
quiz.explain: A deposit moves money between cash and bank; it is neither income nor a cost.

quiz.q: What does the running balance formula =F2+D3-E3 do?
options: Adds all deposits for the month
Adds today's money in to the previous balance and subtracts today's money out
Calculates VAT
Compares the bank and cash books
quiz.explain: Each row takes the balance above, adds the inflow and deducts the outflow.

quiz.q: In a bank reconciliation, how is a deposit made on the last evening of the month treated?
options: Subtracted from the bank book
Ignored until next month
Recorded as income again
Added to the statement balance as a deposit in transit
quiz.explain: The bank has not credited it yet, so it is added to the statement balance to reach the adjusted balance.

quiz.q: Bank charges of ETB 185 appear only on the statement. What should the bookkeeper do?
options: List them as an outstanding check
Ask the bank to remove them
Enter them in the bank book and expense tracker before finishing the reconciliation
Leave them as a permanent difference
quiz.explain: Statement-only items are recorded in your books first; then only timing items remain.

quiz.q: The petty cash float is ETB 5,000 and vouchers since the last top-up total ETB 1,850. How much cash should be in the tin?
quiz.explain: Under the imprest system cash + vouchers = float, so cash = 5,000 - 1,850 = ETB 3,150.

modules.title: Monitoring Your Business Performance
modules.summary: Use the workbook to read daily sales, monitor expenses against budget, track the cash balance week by week, keep on top of amounts owed and run a monthly review that leads to decisions.
objectives: Read the daily sales report with AVERAGE, MAX and MIN and spot patterns and problems
Compare actual expenses with the budget and explain the variances
Track the weekly cash position with SUMIFS by date against a minimum cash buffer
List the month's amounts owed and their due dates, and run a monthly review that ends in decisions

lessons.title: Daily sales reports
body: The daily sales report is the owners' fastest view of the business. A few formulas on the Summary sheet turn it into insight: =COUNT(DailySales!A2:A40) for trading days, =AVERAGE(DailySales!D2:D40) for average daily sales, =MAX(...) and =MIN(...) for the best and lowest days, and =INDEX(DailySales!A2:A40,MATCH(C71,DailySales!D2:D40,0)) to show the date of the best day.

Look at the report every evening and the pattern every week. Which days are strong or weak? What share of customers pay by transfer? Are shortages on particular days? Compare weeks of the same length, because a three-day week will always look smaller than a six-day week.

visual.caption: Bereket's counter sales including VAT in its three full trading weeks of Hidar: steady at about ETB 47,000 a week.

worked.title: Bereket's daily sales, Hidar 2019
worked.note: A useful target for Tahsas: average daily counter sales above ETB 8,000, with the Genna and graduation season helping.

example.title: What the two shortages had in common
example.text: Reviewing the report, Tsion noticed that both shortages, on 19 November and 3 December, were on days when Mahlet was also taking large print orders alone at lunchtime. The owners agreed that Rahel covers the counter from 12:00 to 14:00 and that a mid-day cash count is done on busy days. There were no shortages in the following four weeks.

lessons.title: Expense monitoring against budget
body: A budget is the owners' plan for each cost. On the Summary sheet each expense account has a budget in column C, the actual from SUMIFS in column D, the variance =C13-D13 (negative means over budget) and the share used =IF(C13=0,"",D13/C13). Conditional formatting turns anything over 100% red.

A variance is a question, not a verdict. Ask why: a price rise, more volume (more sales need more paper), a one-off item, waste, or simply a budget that was set too low. Then decide: accept it, act on it, or change next month's budget.

worked.title: Bereket's budget against actual, Hidar 2019

rows.label: 5010 Paper, toner and materials: budget 45,000, actual 52,650
All costs and expenses: budget 166,165, actual 174,730

worked.note: Most of the overspend is on paper and stationery, which were bought partly as opening stock and are still on the shelves. A stock count shows whether they were used or only stored.

scenario.title: Cut the paper orders?
scenario.situation: Kidus sees paper and materials at 117% of budget and tells Tsion to cancel the next Tabor Paper order. Printing sales were strong, and the shelves still hold several cartons of A4 bought in the opening week.
scenario.question: What should Tsion propose?
options: Cancel the order as Kidus says, since the budget is fixed
Count the paper stock and compare paper used with printing sales before deciding; adjust the order to what stock and sales need
Ignore the variance, because sales were good
Raise the printing price by 17% to cover the overspend
scenario.explain: The overspend may be stock not yet used. A count and a comparison with sales show whether there is waste, a price rise or simply opening stock; cancelling blindly risks running out, and a price rise needs its own decision.

lessons.title: Cash balance tracking
body: Owners need to know the cash on hand at any date, not just at month end. The balance at a date is all money in up to that date minus all money out: on the Summary sheet, =SUMIFS(BankBook!$D$2:$D$500,BankBook!$A$2:$A$500,"<="&$A48)-SUMIFS(BankBook!$E$2:$E$500,BankBook!$A$2:$A$500,"<="&$A48) gives the bank balance at the date in A48. The same pattern on CashBook and PettyCash gives the other two, and a line chart shows the trend.

Set a minimum cash buffer, for example one month of rent and payroll, and flag any week below it with =IF(E48<$C$45,"Below buffer","OK"). Remember that part of the cash already belongs to others: VAT collected, PAYE, pension and withholding still to be paid.

lessons.title: Amounts owed and the monthly compliance calendar
body: The month is not closed until you know what is owed and when. VAT returns are monthly: VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024 requires the return and any payment by the last day of the month after the tax period. PAYE withheld from salaries is paid by the end of the following month, and pension contributions (employee 7% and employer 11%) within 30 days after the end of the month in which salary is paid.

A VAT credit does not remove the duty to file. When input VAT is higher than output VAT, as in Bereket's first month because of the copier, the excess is carried forward to the next period; a refund can generally be requested only after six periods of carry-forward. Withholding tax deducted from suppliers must also be remitted; confirm its deadline with your accountant.

items.label: By 14 Dec

items.label: Within the confirmed deadline
items.text: Remit withholding tax of ETB 6,600

items.label: By 8 Jan (Tahsas 30)

regulation.source: VAT Proclamation No. 1341/2024, Arts. 2(1), 48, 58(1) and 59(1); Private Organization Employees' Pension Proclamation No. 1268/2022, Arts. 10 and 12(2)
regulation.text: The VAT tax period is each calendar month; the return and payment are due by the last day of the following month. Excess input credit is carried forward, with a refund request possible after six periods. Employers contribute 11% and employees 7% of salary, paid within 30 days after the end of the month in which salary is paid.

scenario.title: "We have a credit, so we skip the return"
scenario.situation: On 2 January Kidus tells Tsion there is no need to file Hidar's VAT return because Bereket has a credit of ETB 16,502.60 and owes nothing.
scenario.question: What should Tsion reply?
options: The return must still be filed by 8 January (Tahsas 30); the credit is carried forward to Tahsas through the return
Agree, since no payment is due
File it only when the credit is used up
Ask the tax office for a refund of ETB 16,502.60 instead of filing
scenario.explain: A VAT return is due every month whatever the result, and the credit is carried forward through it. A refund can generally be requested only after six periods of carry-forward, so the return is the way to protect the credit.

lessons.title: The monthly review
body: The monthly review turns records into decisions. First close the month: all documents entered, cash and petty cash counted, the bank reconciled, payroll figures entered, and every check on the Summary sheet showing 0. Then the owners look at five things: sales, profit estimate, budget variances, cash position and amounts owed, and decide two or three actions with an owner and a date.

Keep it short and regular, within five working days of month end, and keep a one-page record of the decisions. Over the months the same page shows whether actions worked, and it becomes the history a bank or investor will want to see.

items.text: Entries complete, counts done, bank reconciled

items.label: Check
items.text: Every control check on Summary shows 0

items.label: Read
items.text: Sales, profit, variances, cash and amounts owed

items.label: Decide
items.text: Two or three actions, each with an owner and a date

items.label: Record
items.text: One-page minutes signed by the owners

rows.label: Income before VAT | profit estimate | profit margin
Materials and stock as % of income
Open items

worked.note: Decisions: count stock on the last day of Tahsas; Rahel covers the counter at lunch; Meseret settles IOU-001 by Tahsas 15; prepare Genna and graduation order flyers.

example.title: A youth enterprise's first review
example.text: Four graduates running a car-wash cooperative in Adama started monthly reviews with their microfinance loan officer. The first review showed that water and detergent were 35% of income, far above their plan, because hoses were left running. A ETB 1,200 spray nozzle and a simple daily meter reading cut the cost by a third the next month.

lessons.title: Protecting and improving your system
body: Your workbook is now one of the business's most valuable assets. Save it in a shared folder or cloud drive with automatic backup, keep a dated copy at each month end (for example bereket-books-2019-03-hidar.xlsx), protect the sheets, and give a password only to the people who need it. Never keep the only copy on one laptop or flash disk.

Improve the system one step at a time: add a stock count sheet, a customer orders list or a supplier list when the business needs them, and keep the chart of accounts stable. When the business grows, the same disciplined records make it easy to move to accounting software and to the financial statements, budgets and ratios of the Intermediate course.
points: Month-end copy saved with the month in the file name
Automatic backup to a second location
Formula cells locked and sheets protected
One person responsible, one person reviewing

scenario.title: The stolen laptop
scenario.situation: Tsion's laptop is stolen from a minibus in Tahsas. The workbook was saved on its desktop, with the last backup on a flash disk from Hidar's month end. Paper documents for Tahsas are filed in the office.
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Start a new workbook from today and skip the missing weeks
Estimate Tahsas totals from memory to save time
Restore the Hidar copy, re-enter Tahsas from the filed documents and bank statement, and set up automatic cloud backup with a password
Ask the bank to prepare Bereket's books
scenario.explain: Because every entry has a filed document, the records can be rebuilt exactly. Skipping or estimating weeks would leave gaps in sales, VAT and cash records, and the bank does not keep a business's books.

takeaways: Read the daily sales report every day; compare weeks of the same length and investigate shortages
Budget against actual by account: a variance is a question to answer before acting
Track the cash position by date with SUMIFS and keep it above a minimum buffer, remembering what is owed
File VAT every month even with a credit; pay PAYE by month end and pension within 30 days
Close, check, read, decide and record: a short monthly review within five days of month end

quiz.q: Which formula gives the average daily sales on the Summary sheet?
options: =SUM(DailySales!D2:D40)
=MAX(DailySales!D2:D40)
=AVERAGE(DailySales!D2:D40)
=COUNT(DailySales!D2:D40)
quiz.explain: AVERAGE ignores the blank rows because the row formulas return "" when no date is entered.

quiz.q: The repairs budget is ETB 1,000 and actual is ETB 1,900. What does =C21-D21 show, and what does it mean?
options: -900: repairs are ETB 900 over budget
900: repairs are under budget
190%: repairs are on budget
1,900: the actual cost
quiz.explain: Variance = budget - actual = 1,000 - 1,900 = -900, so the cost is over budget by ETB 900.

quiz.q: How do you calculate the bank balance at a given date in A48?
options: The last number in the balance column
Total deposits for the whole month
The bank statement balance for the month
SUMIFS of deposits dated on or before A48 minus SUMIFS of payments dated on or before A48
quiz.explain: All money in up to the date minus all money out up to the date gives the balance at that date.

quiz.q: When is Hidar's VAT return due?
options: Within 7 days of month end
Only at the end of the fiscal year
By the last day of Tahsas, the following month
Only if VAT is payable
quiz.explain: The return and payment are due by the last day of the month after the tax period, even when there is a credit.

quiz.q: Within what time must employer and employee pension contributions be paid?
options: Within 30 days after the end of the month in which salary is paid
By the end of the fiscal year
Within 7 days of payday
Within 4 months
quiz.explain: Art. 12(2) of Proclamation No. 1268/2022 sets 30 days after the end of the salary month.

quiz.q: What should happen before the owners read the monthly figures?
options: Print every sheet
Send the figures to the bank
Change the budget to match actuals
Close the month and make sure every control check on the Summary shows 0
quiz.explain: Figures are only worth reading once entries are complete, counts and reconciliation are done and the checks agree.

simulation.title: A month as bookkeeper at Bereket Printing and Stationery PLC
setting: You are Tsion Bekele, bookkeeper at Bereket Printing and Stationery PLC, a new printing, photocopy and stationery shop in Piassa, Hawassa. The company has two members, Meseret Alemayehu (managing director, 70%) and her brother Kidus (30%), six staff, ETB 600,000 of share capital and a current account at Bank A, Hawassa branch. It is VAT-registered and finished its first month, Hidar 2019, with a profit estimate of ETB 19,452.60.

This is your second month: Tahsas 2019, from 10 December 2026 to 8 January 2027, with the Genna and graduation season bringing extra orders. You keep the Excel bookkeeping workbook, the cash book, bank book and petty cash book, and you report to Meseret. Mahlet Girma is the cashier, Rahel Yohannes keeps petty cash, and Ato Yared Wolde, an external AABE-registered accountant, prepares the payroll, the tax returns and the accounts.

Items reach you in the order they arrive. Some need a calculation, some need courage. Work as the course teaches: no document, no entry; the company's money is not the owners' money; and every deadline is met.

authority.title: The rules you work under

rows.label: Cash box
rows.value: ETB 3,000 change float; all other cash deposited at Bank A at least every three trading days; daily count by the cashier, checked by you

rows.label: Petty cash
rows.value: Imprest float ETB 5,000 kept by Rahel; maximum ETB 1,000 per voucher; top-up equals approved vouchers

rows.label: Payments
rows.value: Suppliers paid by transfer or check against an approved invoice; Meseret alone up to ETB 20,000, both members above

rows.label: Owners' cash
rows.value: Only against a signed IOU recorded under account 1200 and reported to both members

rows.label: Cash limit (No. 1395/2025)
rows.value: Cash payments above ETB 50,000 per transaction, per day with one person, or per event go through the bank; cash above the limit is not deductible

rows.label: Withholding (No. 1395/2025)
rows.value: 3% on goods above ETB 20,000 and services above ETB 10,000 (30% if no TIN or license); the accountant confirms each amount

rows.label: VAT (No. 1341/2024)
rows.value: 15%; input VAT only on a valid tax invoice; monthly return by the last day of the next month, even with a credit

rows.label: Payroll
rows.value: PAYE by the end of the following month; pension 11% employer and 7% employee within 30 days after the salary month (No. 1268/2022)

rows.label: Receipts (No. 1434/2026)
rows.value: A receipt for every sale; ETB 100,000 non-waivable penalty per invoice not issued

authority.note: Bereket's rules are fictional teaching rules based on the course. In your own business, its written policies and your accountant's advice come first.

meters.label: Record accuracy
meters.help: Rises when entries match documents and checks show 0; falls with guesses, hidden differences and wrong codes.

meters.label: Cash control
meters.help: Rises when cash, bank and petty cash are counted, reconciled and protected; falls when money moves without control.

meters.label: Tax and legal compliance
meters.help: Rises when VAT, withholding, payroll and cash rules are respected; falls sharply with breaches and missed deadlines.

meters.label: Owner and team trust
meters.help: Rises when you explain clearly and solve problems fairly; falls with blame, surprises or blind obedience that later backfires.

tasks.subject: Hidar bank statement: please send the reconciliation
body: Ato Yared forwards Bank A's Hidar statement and asks for the bank reconciliation before he closes Hidar's books. He needs one adjusted figure for the bank account.
Your bank book shows the last deposit, DS-08, made on the evening of 9 December. Check No. 000004 to Tabor Paper was handed over on 8 December.

exhibit.title: Bank A, Hawassa branch: Hidar figures

rows.label: Balance per bank book (before statement items)
Deposit DS-08, credited by the bank on 10 December
Check No. 000004 to Tabor Paper, not yet presented
Service and SMS charges on the statement only

tasks.ask: What do you send Ato Yared?

options.text: Enter the ETB 185 charges first, then report 395,530 + 16,540 - 18,400 = 393,670, which equals the bank book after charges.
options.outcome: The reconciliation agrees to the birr. Statement-only items go into your books first and only timing items remain, as Module 5 teaches.

options.text: Report a difference of ETB 1,675 between the statement and the bank book, and ask the Bank A branch to explain where the money went.
options.outcome: The ETB 1,675 is only timing items and charges, all visible in the exhibit. The bank cannot explain your own deposit in transit and check; a reconciliation starts by listing them.

options.text: Change the bank book balance to the statement's ETB 395,530 so the two agree, and note on the file that the bank's figure is correct and the book was out of date.
options.outcome: Forcing the book to the statement hides a check that has not cleared and a deposit not yet credited. Next month the check will clear and the books will be ETB 18,400 wrong.

options.text: Report the adjusted bank balance as ETB 393,670 against a book of ETB 393,855, and list the ETB 185 as a difference to clear in Tahsas.
options.outcome: The timing items are right, but a known charge left unrecorded keeps the books wrong for a month. Enter statement-only items before you report.

tasks.subject: "A buyer will pay ETB 350,000 into the shop account"
body: Kidus is selling his private car. The buyer wants to pay by bank transfer and Kidus does not have a Bank A account. He asks you to give the buyer Bereket's account number: "The money will only pass through. You can send it to me next week."
Bereket's money policy says the company account is used only for the company's business.

options.text: Say the company account is for Bereket's business only and suggest his own account; if money arrives anyway, record it as owed to him and return it.
options.outcome: You keep personal and company money apart and still help Kidus. A ETB 350,000 private receipt in the company account would distort the bank record and raise questions from the tax authority and the bank, as Module 1 explains.

options.text: Agree, record the ETB 350,000 as a loan from Kidus to the company in the bank book, and repay it by transfer when he asks for it next week.
options.outcome: Recording it is better than hiding it, but it is not a loan: it is Kidus's private sale using the company's account. The company's bank history now shows a large receipt that has nothing to do with its business.

options.text: Agree, and record nothing in the workbook, because the money belongs to Kidus and will leave the account again within a few days.
options.outcome: The bank book would no longer match the bank, and the reconciliation would show ETB 350,000 of unexplained money. Unrecorded private money in a company account is exactly what separation of finances prevents.

options.text: Tell Kidus you need Meseret's approval first, call her before giving the buyer any account number, and then follow whatever the two members decide together.
options.outcome: Escalating is sensible, but you already know the policy: the company account is for company business. Give the clear answer and an alternative, rather than passing the decision on.

tasks.subject: ETB 1,200 short at the cash count
body: Mahlet finishes the count and the daily sales report shows ETB 1,200 short. She is close to tears: "It was a crazy day with the graduation banners. I will put ETB 1,200 of my own money in so the report balances. Please do not tell Meseret."
You open the merchant app for today's transfers before deciding.

exhibit.title: Daily sales report and merchant app, 14 December

rows.label: Received by transfer or mobile, as entered by Mahlet
Merchant app: total transfers received today

options.text: Correct the transfers to ETB 4,140 from the merchant app: expected cash is then 9,860 - 4,140 = 5,720, equal to the count, so nothing is short.
options.outcome: A ETB 1,200 transfer was rung up as cash. Checking the merchant report first, as Module 5 teaches, turns a painful shortage into a recording correction, and Mahlet keeps her money.

options.text: Record a ETB 1,200 cash shortage in account 6950 on an internal voucher signed by Mahlet, and report it to Meseret first thing tomorrow morning before opening.
options.outcome: Honest, but wrong: the money is in the bank, not missing. Always compare the merchant report before accepting a shortage, or you record a loss that never happened and blame the cashier for it.

options.text: Accept Mahlet's ETB 1,200 into the cash box tonight so the report balances, and agree to keep it between the two of you this time.
options.outcome: Mahlet pays for a transfer the customer already made, the bank will show ETB 1,200 more than your records, and a hidden arrangement undermines every future count.

options.text: Raise the cash counted figure to ETB 6,920 so the report balances tonight, and look into the difference properly later in the week.
options.outcome: Changing a counted figure falsifies the record the whole cash system depends on. The true cause was one look at the merchant app away.

tasks.from: Sales representative, Hawassa Office Machines PLC
tasks.subject: Laminating and binding machine: "cheaper in cash"
body: Meseret has approved buying a laminating and binding machine for the graduation season. The supplier's representative offers two prices and says the cash price is "a special Genna discount". He wants your answer today.
Ato Yared has told you that withholding on supplier payments is 3% of the price before VAT for goods above ETB 20,000.

exhibit.title: Two ways to pay for the machine

rows.label: By bank transfer, with a tax invoice: price before VAT
VAT at 15% on the tax invoice
In cash, with a plain receipt and no tax invoice

tasks.ask: How do you arrange the payment?

options.text: Pay by transfer against the tax invoice: ETB 69,000 less ETB 1,800 withholding (3% of 60,000), so the supplier gets ETB 67,200; the VAT is input credit.
options.outcome: The real cost is ETB 60,000 because the VAT is recoverable, against ETB 64,000 in cash with no VAT credit, a breach of the ETB 50,000 rule and no tax deduction. The "discount" was the most expensive option.

options.text: Take the ETB 64,000 cash price, which saves ETB 5,000 on the invoice total, and record the machine as equipment from the supplier's cash receipt.
options.outcome: A ETB 64,000 cash payment breaks the ETB 50,000 rule, is not deductible and has no tax invoice, so no input VAT. Comparing the cash price with a VAT-inclusive total is the trap.

options.text: Pay the full ETB 69,000 by transfer against the tax invoice, because withholding is the supplier's own tax matter and not Bereket's responsibility.
options.outcome: Paying through the bank with a tax invoice is right, but a company must withhold 3% on goods above ETB 20,000. The ETB 1,800 now has to be recovered from the supplier or paid by Bereket.

options.text: Pay by transfer against the tax invoice, but hold the payment until Ato Yared confirms the withholding amount in writing, even if delivery slips by two days.
options.outcome: Safe and compliant, but you already had the rule and the figures to calculate ETB 1,800 yourself. Confirming is good practice; delaying the season's machine was not needed.

tasks.subject: "Give me ETB 15,000 from the till for Genna"
body: Meseret asks for ETB 15,000 from the cash box for family Genna shopping. "Write it as a stationery purchase, it is simpler. It is my company anyway."
IOU-001 for ETB 6,000 from Hidar is still unpaid. The money policy, signed by both members, says owners take cash only against a signed IOU recorded under account 1200 and reported to both members.

options.text: Give it only against a signed IOU under 1200, show her that her IOUs would total ETB 21,000, and tell Kidus as the policy requires.
options.outcome: The company's money is not the owner's money, even for a 70% owner. Recording it truthfully protects Meseret too: Ato Yared can advise on settling the IOUs through payroll or a declared dividend, as Module 1 explains.

options.text: Record the ETB 15,000 under 5020 Stationery as she asks: she is the managing director, she owns 70% of the company and the cash is her decision.
options.outcome: A false expense without an invoice understates profit and misstates the tax records, and under No. 1434/2026 managers are presumed liable. Obeying the instruction does not protect either of you.

options.text: Give her the cash now and record nothing until after Genna, when she can tell you whether she will repay it or not.
options.outcome: The cash box will not agree with the cash book tonight, and an unrecorded withdrawal is easily forgotten. Record it the moment the cash leaves.

options.text: Refuse to release any cash from the till and ask her to transfer money from her own account instead, as the policy prefers.
options.outcome: The money stays safe, but the policy allows a recorded IOU. A flat refusal to the managing director damages the working relationship when a correct recorded route exists.

tasks.subject: Paid ETB 1,800 for the copier repair, no receipt
body: The copier jammed on Monday evening with a school order due. Biruk called a technician he knows, who fixed it for ETB 1,800 in cash. Biruk paid from his own pocket. The technician has no receipt book and is not VAT-registered.
Biruk asks to be repaid from petty cash today. The petty cash limit is ETB 1,000 per voucher.

options.text: Write an internal voucher with the technician's name, phone and ID, get Meseret's approval, and repay Biruk ETB 1,800 from the cash box, with no VAT.
options.outcome: An approved internal voucher supports the cost when the receipt is genuinely missing, and paying above the petty cash limit from the cash box with approval follows the rules. It never supports input VAT, as Module 3 teaches.

options.text: Repay him ETB 1,800 from petty cash on two vouchers of ETB 900 each, so that each voucher stays within the ETB 1,000 petty cash limit.
options.outcome: Biruk is repaid, but splitting one payment to fit a limit defeats the control. Above-limit payments need approval, not two vouchers.

options.text: Ask the technician to write a tax invoice dated today with 15% VAT added on top of the ETB 1,800, so Bereket can claim ETB 270 of input VAT on the repair.
options.outcome: A technician who is not VAT-registered cannot issue a tax invoice, and adding VAT that was never charged creates a false credit. That is a serious breach, not a saving.

options.text: Repay him ETB 1,800 from the cash box today on Meseret's word, and write the voucher details for the technician at month end.
options.outcome: Fair to Biruk, but the details are easiest to get today and month end is when they get lost. Prepare the internal voucher before the cash leaves.

tasks.subject: Tahsas income looks too low
body: Preparing a mid-month update, you see that the Summary sheet's total income is lower than the daily sales report and the order invoices together. The Genna orders have pushed the Income sheet to row 75.
The income formulas on the Summary were copied from an early draft.

rows.label: Summary E10: total income including VAT
DailySales D41: counter sales including VAT
Order invoices INV-0005 to INV-0019 including VAT

options.text: Rewrite the formulas with fixed ranges to row 500 and the month's date criteria, copy them to every account, and check the total reaches ETB 263,700.
options.outcome: Rows 61 to 75 (ETB 74,100) were outside the range. Fixed ranges to row 500 with dates from B2 and B3 work every month without editing, as Module 4 shows.

options.text: Type the missing ETB 74,100 into the total cell by hand for Tahsas and add a cell comment explaining the adjustment for Ato Yared.
options.outcome: The total looks right today, but a typed number breaks the link to the data and must be redone every month. Fix the formula, not the result.

options.text: Delete the oldest rows of the Income sheet so that all of the remaining Tahsas entries fit inside rows 2 to 60, which the formula already reads correctly.
options.outcome: Deleting records to suit a formula destroys the evidence for sales and VAT. The formula must fit the data, never the other way round.

options.text: Extend the ranges in each formula to row 75 now, and remember to extend them again whenever the Income sheet grows past that row.
options.outcome: It works today, but the next busy month will break it again. Ranges to row 500 with the date criteria solve it once.

tasks.subject: Weekly petty cash count
body: You count the petty cash tin with Rahel before the holiday weekend and ask her for the vouchers paid since the last top-up.
Rahel says she does not remember anything unusual this week.

rows.label: Vouchers PCV-014 to PCV-019 since the last top-up

options.text: Recount and look for a missing voucher; if none, record ETB 200 short on an internal voucher Meseret approves, then top up ETB 2,550.
options.outcome: Cash 2,450 + vouchers 2,350 = 4,800, so ETB 200 is unexplained. A recount and search come first; a real shortage is recorded and approved, and the float is restored, as the imprest system in Module 5 requires.

options.text: Top up ETB 2,550 to bring the tin back to ETB 5,000 and note the ETB 200 difference as rounding on this week's petty cash sheet.
options.outcome: A ETB 200 gap on a ETB 5,000 float is not rounding. Writing it off without a search or approval hides whatever caused it.

options.text: Top up ETB 2,350 against the vouchers and say nothing about the difference, since ETB 200 is too small to raise before a holiday.
options.outcome: The float silently becomes ETB 4,800 and next week's count will not balance either. Small differences are the early warning the count exists to catch.

options.text: Record the ETB 200 as a shortage, tell Rahel that it will be deducted from her next salary, and top up ETB 2,550 to restore the ETB 5,000 float.
options.outcome: The record is right, but a salary deduction is the owners' decision after a fair look at the facts, not the bookkeeper's. Report it to Meseret instead.

tasks.subject: "We made ETB 128,000. Let us pay ourselves ETB 100,000"
body: Kidus has looked at the bank app: "Cash and bank went up by ETB 128,000 in Tahsas. That is our profit. Please prepare a transfer of ETB 100,000 to Meseret and me before Genna."
Your draft Tahsas summary is in the exhibit. Salaries were paid on 4 January for Tahsas; PAYE and pension are due next month.

rows.label: Materials, stock and other costs before VAT (excluding salaries)
PAYE and employee pension withheld, not yet paid
Increase in cash and bank in Tahsas

options.text: Explain that the profit estimate is ETB 105,235, not the ETB 128,000 rise in cash, and that a dividend needs a members' decision, advice and 15% withholding.
options.outcome: 284,000 - 121,600 - 39,645 - 11,855 - 5,665 = ETB 105,235. Cash includes VAT collected and payroll owed, so it is not profit, as Module 2 explains, and dividends follow a proper decision and tax.

options.text: Confirm a profit of ETB 162,400 (income less costs), because the salaries have already gone out of the bank and are inside the ETB 128,000.
options.outcome: Salaries are a cost of the month whether or not they are in the bank figure. Leaving out ETB 57,165 of payroll overstates profit by more than half.

options.text: Agree that profit is the ETB 128,000 rise in cash and bank, and prepare the ETB 100,000 transfer to the two members today so that Meseret can approve it before Genna.
options.outcome: Cash growth is not profit, and an informal transfer to members is neither a salary nor a declared dividend. It would strip cash needed for VAT, PAYE and pension.

options.text: Send Kidus the profit estimate of ETB 105,235 and leave the dividend question entirely to the two members without any comment from you.
options.outcome: The figure is right, but Kidus asked for a transfer. A bookkeeper should point out that a dividend needs a members' decision, advice and withholding.

tasks.subject: Paper costs 38% over budget
body: In the pre-review meeting Meseret points at the paper line: "ETB 69,000 against a budget of ETB 50,000. Someone is wasting paper. What do we do?"
You have the figures in the exhibit ready.

exhibit.title: Paper and toner, Tahsas to 6 January

rows.label: Printing and copying sales before VAT, against Hidar
Tabor Paper price per ream: Hidar | Tahsas
Cartons of A4 on the shelves: 10 December | today

options.text: Explain it: about 10% is higher sales and 10.5% the price rise, the rest is stock grown from 6 to 14 cartons; order to sales and get a second quote.
options.outcome: A variance is a question, as Module 6 teaches. Volume and price explain part of it; most of the rest is cash sitting on the shelves, so the fix is ordering to need and testing the supplier's price.

options.text: Cancel the next Tabor Paper order completely and tell the print team that paper use must fall back to the ETB 50,000 budget at once.
options.outcome: There is stock to use, but blaming the team and cancelling blindly ignores higher sales and the price rise. You risk running out in the busy graduation weeks.

options.text: Raise printing and copying prices by 38% from next week, so that the extra paper cost is fully covered by the shop's customers.
options.outcome: Most of the overspend is stock, not a lasting cost increase. A 38% price rise would drive customers to competitors to cover cartons still on the shelves.

options.text: Raise the paper budget to ETB 69,000 from Hidar's ETB 50,000 for the coming months, since this month's actual figure shows what the busy shop really needs.
options.outcome: Setting the budget to this month's actual builds the extra stock into every future month. Find the causes first.

tasks.subject: Today is the deadline
body: Ato Yared reminds you that today is the last day for Hidar's VAT return and for Hidar's PAYE and pension. Meseret, on the other line, says: "We have a VAT credit, so skip that return, and let us pay PAYE and pension next week when the Genna order money arrives."
The bank book shows ETB 452,300 this morning.

options.text: All three are due today: file the Hidar return to carry the ETB 16,502.60 credit forward, and pay PAYE ETB 8,250 and pension ETB 9,270 from the bank.
options.outcome: The cash is there and the deadlines are fixed. A credit return still has to be filed, and late pension brings interest plus a 5% monthly penalty, as Module 6 and the owners' duties in Module 2 explain.

options.text: Skip the VAT return because nothing is payable this month, and pay PAYE and pension next week when the Genna order receipts clear, as Meseret prefers.
options.outcome: Two breaches in one decision: a missing return and late payroll taxes, with more than enough money in the bank. Managers are presumed liable under No. 1434/2026.

options.text: File the VAT return today, but pay the pension next week, since the late-payment penalty on ETB 9,270 for a few days will be small.
options.outcome: Pension paid late attracts interest and a 5% monthly penalty under No. 1268/2022, and staff contributions are not the business's to hold. With ETB 452,300 in the bank there is no reason to wait.

options.text: Pay PAYE and pension today, and file the VAT return next week, since a return with a credit and no tax due carries little risk.
options.outcome: The payments are right, but the return is still due today. Filing it is how the ETB 16,502.60 credit is carried forward.

followUps.subject: ETB 1,200 more in the bank than in your records
body: Checking the weekly statement, Ato Yared sees that the merchant account received ETB 4,140 on 14 December, while your daily sales report shows ETB 2,940 of transfers and no shortage that day.
He asks you to explain the ETB 1,200 before he reconciles the bank.

options.text: Explain what happened, correct the 14 December report to ETB 4,140 of transfers, return any money Mahlet put in, and add a daily merchant-app check.
options.outcome: Owning the mistake and fixing both the record and the cause restores trust. The merchant check would have shown the answer on the night.

options.text: Tell Ato Yared it is probably a small rounding or timing difference at Bank A and ask him to carry it forward to the January reconciliation.
options.outcome: ETB 1,200 is a specific amount with a specific cause. Misleading the accountant turns a recording slip into a trust problem.

options.text: Correct the 14 December report quietly without mentioning the cash arrangement, so that the figures agree and nobody is upset.
options.outcome: The figures are fixed, but Mahlet's ETB 1,200 is still in the cash box and the owners do not know why. Corrections need an explanation.

followUps.subject: The ETB 64,000 cash payment
body: Ato Yared has found the ETB 64,000 cash payment for the laminating machine. He explains that it breaks the ETB 50,000 cash limit, is not deductible and has no tax invoice, so there is no input VAT.
He asks how you want to deal with it.

options.text: Tell Meseret plainly, record the machine as equipment paid in cash and non-deductible, and propose that all payments above ETB 20,000 go by transfer.
options.outcome: The breach cannot be undone, but honest records and a clear rule stop it recurring. The owners can see what the "discount" really cost.

options.text: Re-record the payment as two cash payments of ETB 32,000 dated on different days, so that each of them appears to stay safely below the ETB 50,000 cash limit in the books.
options.outcome: Changing dates to hide a breach falsifies the books. It would turn a mistake into deliberate misreporting.

options.text: Leave the entry exactly as it is and move on, since the machine is already bought and nothing can be changed now.
options.outcome: The entry may stand, but the owners need to know the cost and the business needs a rule, or the next supplier offer will repeat it.

followUps.subject: ETB 15,000 of stationery with no invoice
body: Ato Yared finds an ETB 15,000 stationery purchase on 19 December with no invoice, no supplier and no stock received. He asks what it is before he prepares the VAT return.

options.text: Tell him the truth, correct the entry to account 1200 Due from shareholders, ask Meseret to sign an IOU, and inform Kidus.
options.outcome: Correcting it before month end keeps the accounts and returns true. Meseret's balance with the company is now visible and can be settled properly.

options.text: Ask a friend's stationery shop in Piassa for an invoice of ETB 15,000 dated 19 December, so the entry has a supporting document behind it.
options.outcome: A false invoice is tax fraud, with heavy penalties under No. 1434/2026. A document must prove a real transaction.

options.text: Tell him it was a stationery purchase paid in cash and that the receipt was lost, and leave the entry under 5020.
options.outcome: The story will not survive a stock check, and the accountant now prepares returns on a false figure.

followUps.subject: Missed return and late payroll taxes
body: Ato Yared reports that Hidar's VAT return was not filed and that PAYE and pension were paid nine days late. Late-payment interest and penalties apply, and the pension fund will add a 5% monthly penalty.

options.text: File the return now, pay the interest and penalties as assessed, record them as non-deductible, and put every deadline in a shared calendar.
options.outcome: Correcting quickly limits the cost, and a calendar with reminders prevents a repeat. Penalties are recorded honestly, not hidden.

options.text: Wait until the Ministry of Revenues sends a formal notice, then apply for a full waiver of the penalties under the penalty waiver directive.
options.outcome: Waiting adds interest, which is not waivable, and waivers are partial and conditional. File and pay first; ask for relief afterward if it applies.

options.text: Record the penalties as bank charges so the owners do not see a tax penalty line in the monthly summary.
options.outcome: Mislabeling penalties hides a real problem from the owners and misstates the accounts.

memo.prompt: Write a one-page hand-over note to Meseret Alemayehu and Ato Yared Wolde at the end of Tahsas: what the books show for the month, what you corrected and what needs a decision.
guide: The month's figures: income before VAT, profit estimate, cash and bank at month end, and the six control checks.
Two moments where you followed the rules under pressure, with the facts and amounts, and what happened.
Amounts owed and their due dates: VAT, withholding, PAYE, pension and any shareholder IOUs.
One improvement to the system (a check, a calendar, a rule) with an owner and a start date.
Decisions you need from the owners, such as the paper ordering rule or settling the IOUs.

practical.title: My first month's bookkeeping workbook
practical.text: Using the SME bookkeeping workbook, build a complete set of records for one month: either Bereket Printing and Stationery PLC's first month (Hidar 2019) from the course's sample documents, or your own business or project's latest month. Set up the chart of accounts and drop-down lists, enter every day's sales and every payment, keep the cash book, bank book and petty cash book, reconcile the bank, and finish with a monthly summary in which every control check shows 0 and a one-page review with your decisions.
steps: Download sme-bookkeeping-workbook.xlsx, read the Instructions sheet and enter your business details, the month's start and end dates on Summary, and your own chart of accounts (or keep Bereket's 28 accounts)
Set up the drop-down lists and date rules with Data Validation, and check one row of each formula by hand (for example the VAT on ETB 5,980 is ETB 780)
For each trading day, complete one DailySales row after the cash count, the two counter sales rows in Income, and the cash and transfer lines in CashBook and BankBook
Enter every payment in Expenses from its document and in CashBook, BankBook or PettyCash, and clear every message in the Check column
At month end count the cash box and petty cash, record bank charges, enter the statement balance and timing items on BankBook, and enter the payroll figures on Summary
Make sure all six control checks show 0, then complete the budget, cash position and amounts owed, and write a one-page monthly review with two or three decisions
deliverables: The completed workbook for the month, with every control check on the Summary sheet at 0
A signed bank reconciliation and petty cash count for the last day of the month
A one-page monthly review: sales, profit estimate, budget variances, cash position, amounts owed with due dates, and two or three decisions with owners and dates

downloads.label: SME bookkeeping workbook
downloads.note: A ready-to-use, nine-sheet workbook with a chart of accounts, daily sales report, income tracker, expense tracker, cash book, bank book and reconciliation, petty cash book and a monthly summary with budget, weekly cash position, amounts owed and control checks, filled with Bereket's Hidar 2019 sample month.

criteria: Complete all six modules and their quizzes
Pass the workplace simulation with 70% or more
Pass the 20-question final exam with 70% or more
Blended and classroom cohorts: submit the practical exercise, assessed by an Erudite facilitator against the deliverables above
Classroom delivery: attend all four training days in full

exam.q: Meseret and Kidus put ETB 600,000 into their new PLC. Which structure meets the Commercial Code No. 1243/2021?
options: 12,000 shares of ETB 50, fully paid
6,000 shares of ETB 100, fully paid into a blocked bank account before registration
6,000 shares of ETB 100, with 25% paid before registration
No shares, because a PLC has members, not shareholders
exam.explain: A PLC's capital (minimum ETB 15,000) is fully paid at incorporation into a blocked account, with shares of at least ETB 100; 25% payment applies to share companies.

exam.q: Bereket's business license was issued in Tikimt 2019. When must it first be renewed without penalty?
options: Exactly one year after issue, in Tikimt 2020
Every month with the VAT return
Only when the business moves premises
Between Hamle 1, 2019 and Tahsas 30, 2020 E.C. (8 July 2027 to early January 2028)
exam.explain: Licenses run to the end of the fiscal year and are renewed between Hamle 1 and Tahsas 30; a late window from Tir 1 carries penalties.

exam.q: A sole proprietor's annual turnover rises from ETB 1.6 million to ETB 2.4 million. What changes?
options: Nothing, because individuals are always Category B
He pays the old turnover tax at a higher rate
He moves to Category A, must keep full books and must register for VAT
He must convert to a PLC
exam.explain: Individuals above ETB 2,000,000 are Category A, and passing ETB 2,000,000 of taxable supplies, and being Category A, both require VAT registration. Turnover tax was repealed by No. 1395/2025.

exam.q: A customer transfers ETB 9,200 for an order into Meseret's personal account by mistake. What is the best response?
options: Meseret transfers it to the company account the same day, Tsion records it as the order receipt with a note, and the counter shows only the company's account
Leave it in her account and reduce her next salary by ETB 9,200
Record nothing, since the company did not receive it
Record it as a shareholder loan to the company
exam.explain: Company sales belong in the company account and books; moving the money promptly and fixing the cause keeps sales, VAT and the bank record complete.

exam.q: On one day Bereket owes a paper supplier ETB 32,000 and ETB 21,000 on two invoices. The supplier asks for cash. What applies?
options: Each invoice is below ETB 50,000, so cash is fine
The day's total of ETB 53,000 to one person is above ETB 50,000, so both payments go through the bank
Only the ETB 32,000 invoice must go through the bank
Cash is fine if the supplier signs a receipt
exam.explain: The limit applies per transaction, per day with one person and per event, and cash above it is also not deductible.

exam.q: A café receives ETB 11,500 from a customer, including 15% VAT. What is its revenue and its VAT?
options: Revenue ETB 11,500 and VAT ETB 1,725
Revenue ETB 9,775 and VAT ETB 1,725
Revenue ETB 11,500 and no VAT
Revenue ETB 10,000 and VAT ETB 1,500
exam.explain: VAT inside the price is 11,500 x 15 / 115 = ETB 1,500, leaving revenue of ETB 10,000.

exam.q: In a month a shop has income before VAT of ETB 120,000, cost of sales of ETB 45,000 and payments of ETB 50,000 that include a ETB 15,000 laptop. What is its profit estimate?
exam.explain: The laptop is equipment, so expenses are 50,000 - 15,000 = 35,000 and profit is 120,000 - 45,000 - 35,000 = ETB 40,000.

exam.q: Bereket's costs other than materials are ETB 90,580 a month and its contribution ratio is 61%. About what income before VAT does it need to break even?
exam.explain: Break-even = 90,580 / 0.61, about ETB 148,492; multiplying instead of dividing gives the wrong answers.

exam.q: Under the Tax Administration (Amendment) Proclamation No. 1434/2026, who is presumed liable for a business's tax obligations?
options: Its managers and finance heads, including for sole proprietorships
Only the external accountant
Only the bookkeeper who made the entry
Nobody personally, only the company
exam.explain: The amendment presumes managers and finance heads liable, which is why owners must review and approve the figures.

exam.q: A supplier's tax invoice for a Hidar purchase is found only in Megabit, four months later. What is correct?
options: The credit is lost
Change the Hidar return without the invoice
Record the VAT as an expense
Claim the input VAT in Megabit's return, within the 12-month limit for missed credits
exam.explain: The credit moves to the period in which the invoice is held, and missed credits can be claimed within 12 calendar months.

exam.q: A technician repairs the copier for ETB 1,800 and has no receipt. Which record is right?
options: A petty cash voucher marked "VAT included"
Two petty cash vouchers of ETB 900 each
An approved internal voucher with the payee's name, phone, ID and signature, coded to repairs with no input VAT
No record, since there is no receipt
exam.explain: An internal voucher supports the cost but never VAT, and splitting to fit the ETB 1,000 petty cash limit hides an above-limit payment.

exam.q: Which entry is classified correctly in Bereket's chart of accounts?
options: A ETB 46,000 laptop to 1500 Equipment
A cash deposit at Bank A to 4010 Printing income
Meseret's ETB 6,000 IOU to 5020 Stationery
Share capital received to 4090 Other income
exam.explain: Equipment is an asset; deposits are transfers, an owner's IOU is a receivable and capital is equity, never income or cost.

exam.q: How long should an Ethiopian company keep its books and documents?
options: Exactly 5 years from the transaction
Until the license is renewed
Only until the annual return is filed
At least 10 years: the longer of the Commercial Code period and 5 years from filing
exam.explain: Proclamation No. 983/2016 Art. 17(2) requires the longer period; the Commercial Code period for company books is reported as 10 years.

exam.q: In the income tracker G2 holds ETB 6,900. What do H2 =ROUND(G2*15/115,2) and I2 =G2-H2 return?
exam.explain: 6,900 x 15 / 115 = 900, and 6,900 - 900 = 6,000; 1,035 is the common error of taking 15% of the gross.

exam.q: Which Summary formula adds the net cost of account 5010 for the month in B2:B3?
options: =SUMIFS(Expenses!$J$2:$J$500,Expenses!$E$2:$E$500,5010,Expenses!$A$2:$A$500,">="&$B$2,Expenses!$A$2:$A$500,"<="&$B$3)
=SUM(Expenses!J2:J60)
=SUMIFS(Expenses!$E$2:$E$500,Expenses!$J$2:$J$500,5010)
=SUMIFS(Expenses!$L$2:$L$500,Expenses!$E$2:$E$500,"Paper")
exam.explain: The sum range is the net column J, the criteria are the code column E and the date column A; the other formulas sum everything, swap the ranges, use totals with VAT or a text name.

exam.q: Bereket pays a designer ETB 12,000 for a logo (services, net of VAT) with no withholding entered. What does the Check column show?
options: Nothing, because the amount is below ETB 20,000
"Above ETB 50,000: pay through the bank"
"Check withholding", because services above ETB 10,000 need the accountant's review
"No input VAT without a tax invoice"
exam.explain: The formula flags services above ETB 10,000 and goods above ETB 20,000 when column M is 0; the accountant then applies 3% (or 30% without a TIN).

exam.q: At month end: statement ETB 210,000; deposit in transit ETB 14,500; outstanding check ETB 22,000; bank book before charges ETB 202,700; charges on the statement ETB 200. What is the adjusted balance, and does it agree?
options: ETB 246,500, a difference to investigate
ETB 202,500, agreeing with the bank book after recording the ETB 200 charges
ETB 202,700, agreeing without any entry
ETB 217,500, so the bank owes Bereket money
exam.explain: 210,000 + 14,500 - 22,000 = 202,500, and 202,700 - 200 = 202,500, so the books agree once the charges are recorded.

exam.q: The petty cash float is ETB 5,000. The tin holds ETB 2,950 and vouchers since the last top-up total ETB 1,900. What does this show?
options: Everything balances
A top-up of ETB 1,900 restores the float
An overage of ETB 150
An unexplained shortage of ETB 150 to recount, investigate and report
exam.explain: Cash + vouchers = 2,950 + 1,900 = 4,850, which is ETB 150 below the float; it must be explained before topping up.

A shop has ETB 95,000 in cash and bank, owes ETB 17,520 of PAYE and pension and ETB 9,000 of VAT, and sets a minimum buffer of ETB 80,000. What should the owners conclude?
options: Free cash is about ETB 68,480, below the buffer, so hold back non-essential spending
Cash is ETB 15,000 above the buffer, so spending can continue
VAT and PAYE can wait, so the buffer is met
The buffer only applies at year-end
